item.title: Longitudinal viral load trajectories predict cervical lesion risk in women with persistent human papillomavirus infection: A prospective cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Zhou Y, Chen S, Zhang Y, Jiang Y, Xiao M, Xin X, Shi Z, Zhang L
item.description:
Authors: Zhou Y, Chen S, Zhang Y, Jiang Y, Xiao M, Xin X, Shi Z, Zhang L
Journal: Cancer | DOI: 10.1002/cncr.70648
Published: 2026-Dec-01
PMID: 43069728



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is central to cervical lesion development, but single viral-load measurements may not capture heterogeneous viral dynamics. This study characterized longitudinal viral-load trajectories among women with persistent infection and evaluated their associations with cervical lesions and incremental predictive value beyond baseline factors. METHODS: In this prospective cohort of 1502 HPV-positive women followed at approximately 6-month intervals, latent class growth analysis using actual follow-up time was conducted among 624 women with type-specific persistent infection. Associations between trajectory group and any cervical lesion (low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion or high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion [HSIL]) were assessed using multivariable logistic regression; HSIL was explored using Firth-penalized regression. Discrimination, calibration, and decision-curve analysis were used to assess incremental predictive performance. RESULTS: Of 1170 women with classifiable outcomes, 624 had persistent infection. Four trajectories were identified: low stable (39.6%), moderate declining (18.9%), moderate increasing (29.8%), and persistently high (11.7%). Any-lesion prevalence was 10.9%, 17.8%, 74.2%, and 90.4%, respectively (p < .001). Compared with the low-stable group, fully adjusted odds ratios (ORs) were 1.95 (95% CI, 1.02-3.74), 29.66 (95% CI, 16.75-52.51), and 124.29 (95% CI, 47.30-326.60) for the other groups, respectively. The persistently high group was also associated with HSIL (OR, 9.47; 95% CI, 3.18-33.09). The optimism-corrected area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) increased from 0.713 for the base model to 0.888 for both the simple longitudinal and trajectory models and 0.899 for the joint model. CONCLUSIONS: Longitudinal HPV viral-load dynamics identified clinically distinct risk phenotypes. Moderate-increasing and persistently high trajectories were strongly associated with cervical lesions, whereas longitudinal information improved discrimination beyond baseline measurements. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

item.title: Impact of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists on Head and Neck Cancer: Integrated Evidence From TCGA Genomic Analysis and a US Multicenter Database Study.
item.dc:creator: Chen TY, Jin L, Mao PC, Chou CW, Chen HY, Chang R, Li CJ, Liu WS
item.description:
Authors: Chen TY, Jin L, Mao PC, Chou CW, Chen HY, Chang R, Li CJ, Liu WS
Journal: International journal of cancer | DOI: 10.1002/ijc.70805
Published: 2026-Nov-24
PMID: 43079591



Abstract:
Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a risk factor for head and neck cancer (HNC), but the effects of antidiabetic drugs on this risk are unclear. We evaluated glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) versus dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP-4is) or sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) using the TriNetX US electronic health record database, while investigating the molecular role of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP1R) in HNC. Adults ≥ 40 years with newly diagnosed T2DM (2012-2024) were studied retrospectively. Among > 250 million records, 105,605 GLP-1RA users were propensity-score matched 1:1 with 105,605 nonusers. Over a median 5-year follow-up, GLP-1RA use was associated with significantly lower risks of incident HNC (HR: 0.723; 95% CI: 0.617-0.848) and all-cause mortality (HR: 0.737; 95% CI: 0.715-0.759). Results remained consistent across sex, age, obesity, smoking, alcohol use, GLP-1RA type, and further sensitivity analyses. Molecular analyses showed that higher GLP1R expression was associated with better overall survival in The Cancer Genome Atlas Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (TCGA-HNSC). GLP1R expression progressively decreased from normal to tumor and metastatic tissues, correlated with oncogenic mutation status, and was inversely associated with cell-cycle programs. In an independent multi-institutional biobank (Tri-VGH Biobank), GLP1R expression was significantly lower in tumor than matched adjacent non-tumor tissues (27 pairs), findings confirmed by tumor immunofluorescence. Overall, these epidemiological and molecular findings support a potential protective role of GLP-1RA/GLP1R signaling in HNC.

item.title: How We Do It-Free Flap Reconstruction of Cricoid Chondrosarcoma: Preservation of Voice, Airway, and Swallow.
item.dc:creator: Kirke DN, Roof SA, Courey M
item.description:
Authors: Kirke DN, Roof SA, Courey M
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70566
Published: 2026-Nov-24
PMID: 43078569



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: We present our experience with open total cricoid ring resection/partial laryngectomy with free flap reconstruction in the setting of cricoid chondrosarcoma. We aimed to assess whether long-term outcomes yielded appropriate oncologic and functional results to justify avoidance of total laryngectomy. METHODS: Retrospective chart review of patients undergoing open total cricoid ring resection/partial laryngectomy for low to moderate grade cricoid chondrosarcoma. All patients were reconstructed with an autologous rib, wrapped with vascularized fascia harvested from an anterolateral thigh free flap. RESULTS: Five patients (four male and one female) were identified. The median age of diagnosis was 55.2 years (range: 46-62) and average follow-up time was approximately 2.54 years (range: 37-299 weeks). No patient has required a completion laryngectomy. All five (100%) patients are tolerating an oral diet, while four (80%) have been decannulated. CONCLUSIONS: This is an oncologically safe approach and is a functionally viable alternative to total laryngectomy.

item.title: Antibody-Drug Conjugates and Oral Toxicities.
item.dc:creator: Nagarajan N, Brondfield S, Qureshi K, Villa A
item.description:
Authors: Nagarajan N, Brondfield S, Qureshi K, Villa A
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70530
Published: 2026-Nov-24
PMID: 43078522



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) are an emerging and promising class of anticancer therapeutics. This retrospective study aimed to characterize the oral toxicities associated with ADC treatment. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The study was conducted using de-identified clinical data from the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) PatientExploreR database through 2024. A total of 13 ADCs were included in the analysis. Demographic characteristics, cancer diagnoses, treatment data, and oral toxicity data were retrieved for all eligible patients. STATISTICAL ANALYSIS: Descriptive statistics summarized demographic characteristics, smoking status, oral toxicity prevalence, and median time to onset. Associations between oral toxicity categories and sex, race, and smoking status were assessed using Pearson's chi-square or Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact tests. RESULTS: A total of 1144 patients who received ADC therapy were included in the study, including 59.7% females, 15.9% males, and 24.0% unknown. Oral toxicities were recorded in 13.7% of patients, with mucosal lesions being the most prevalent (10.5%), followed by dry mouth (2.3%) and orofacial neuropathies (1.0%). A Pearson's chi-square test demonstrated a significant association between sex at birth and oral toxicity category (p = 0.023). The frequency of oral mucosal lesions varied significantly across the ADCs (Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact test with Monte Carlo simulation, 100 000 replicates; p < 0.0001). The frequency of dry mouth and orofacial neuropathies did not differ significantly among the ADCs (p = 0.412 and 0.297). CONCLUSION: Given the expanding use of ADCs in cancer therapy, characterization of their toxicity profile is essential. In this study, oral toxicities were observed in 13.7% of patients, with oral mucosal lesions being the predominant toxicity, followed by dry mouth.

item.title: Molecular residual disease interception in locoregionally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: The MERIDIAN Phase II trial.
item.dc:creator: Sanz-Garcia E, Spreafico A, Hosni A, de Almeida JR, McPartlin A, Eng L, Goldstein DP, Hope A, Hahn E, Yao C, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Sanz-Garcia E, Spreafico A, Hosni A, de Almeida JR, McPartlin A, Eng L, Goldstein DP, Hope A, Hahn E, Yao C, et al.
Journal: Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research | DOI: 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-26-3112
Published: 2026-Nov-24
PMID: 43077433



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Molecular residual disease (MRD) interception has not been studied in locoregionally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (LA-HNSCC). MERIDIAN evaluates whether rilvegostomig, an anti-PD-1/TIGIT bispecific antibody, could clear ctDNA in MRD setting. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Patients with stage III HPV-positive or stage III-IVB HPV-negative LA-HNSCC received definitive treatment (surgery ± adjuvant therapy, radiation, or chemoradiation). ctDNA was assessed using an exome-based tumor-informed assay at baseline and surveillance. Patients with detectable ctDNA during MRD window (8-12 weeks post-definitive therapy), no progression, and PD-L1 ≥1 were eligible for randomization (3:1) to rilvegostomig or observation. Plasma HPV DNA was evaluated using HPV sequencing. RESULTS: Of 52 enrolled patients, 42 were evaluable; 57% had oropharyngeal cancer (OPC), mostly treated with chemoradiation. Six patients (14%) were ctDNA positive at the MRD window: 3 had progression, 1 had PD-L1 <1, 1 received rilvegostomig, and 1 was observed. The treated MRD-positive patient achieved ctDNA clearance at 10 weeks and remained recurrence-free through 23.4 months of follow-up. The two untreated MRD-positive patients showed substantial lead times to progression (190 and 235 days). Excluding the treated patient, ctDNA positivity at the MRD window was associated with worse RFS (HR 16.9; 95% CI 4.4-64.7) and OS (HR 5.3; 95% CI 1.2-22.2). In HPV-positive OPC, plasma HPV DNA correlated with worse RFS (p=0.02). Combined ctDNA and HPV DNA achieved 100% sensitivity and 73% specificity. CONCLUSIONS: ctDNA detection post-treatment predicts outcomes in LA-HNSCC. MERIDIAN provides preliminary evidence for MRD interception with rilvegostomig, showing durable ctDNA clearance.

item.title: Association between duodenal mucosa-associated periodontal bacteria and advanced liver fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
item.dc:creator: Niida K, Yamamoto Y, Miyake T, Hayashi M, Tange K, Watanabe T, Yoshida O, Tokumoto Y, Tomida H, Takeshita E, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Niida K, Yamamoto Y, Miyake T, Hayashi M, Tange K, Watanabe T, Yoshida O, Tokumoto Y, Tomida H, Takeshita E, et al.
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0363551
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43077432



Abstract:
Gut microbiota and periodontal diseases are potential risk factors for duodenal mucosa-associated microbiota in fibrosis progression of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease; however, the specific contribution of duodenal mucosa-associated microbiota remains unclear. Therefore, in this prospective study, we investigated its association with liver stiffness to elucidate its role in disease progression. Duodenal brush samples were collected during endoscopy from patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, classified by liver stiffness measurement into advanced (liver stiffness measurement>8.7 kPa, n = 10) and non-advanced (n = 20) groups. Extracted DNA was subjected to shotgun metagenomic sequencing. Analyses included taxonomy, diversity, differential abundance (edgeR), correlation (Spearman), and receiver operating characteristic predictive modeling, focusing on periodontal bacteria. While microbial diversity did not differ, advanced metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease was characterized by the enrichment of the phylum Pseudomonadota and the genera Haemophilus and Klebsiella. Eight periodontal bacteria, including Campylobacter rectus, Porphyromonas gingivalis, and Fusobacterium nucleatum, were significantly enriched in patients with advanced metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (P < 0.05) and correlated with liver fibrosis markers. A model based on these bacteria discriminated advanced metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease with an AUC of 0.82 (95% CI, 0.634-1.000). Duodenal mucosa-associated microbiota alterations, particularly the enrichment of eight periodontal species, were associated with fibrosis severity. These findings highlight the role of the oral-gut-liver axis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease progression and suggest potential microbial biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

item.title: In vitro functional evaluation of toothbrushes using two standardized models of the smooth and interproximal surface model.
item.dc:creator: Endoh M, Tsuji Y, Jinushi T, Kurihara S, Higuchi T, Takayanagi A, Yamagishi A, Nomoto T
item.description:
Authors: Endoh M, Tsuji Y, Jinushi T, Kurihara S, Higuchi T, Takayanagi A, Yamagishi A, Nomoto T
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0338683
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43077421



Abstract:
Manual toothbrushes are the most widely used for daily plaque control.　Although proper toothbrushing technique is crucial for effective plaque removal, improving and sustaining these skills remains challenging. Consequently, selecting an appropriate toothbrush is essential for maintaining optimal oral health. Despite various toothbrushes available, objective evaluation of the functional index of a toothbrush remains elusive. This study aimed to develop a comprehensive and objective evaluation method for toothbrush function using standardized models. For comprehensive evaluation, the assessed surface was divided into three elements (convex, concave, and flat). Two standardized evaluation models were developed: the smooth and interproximal surface model, which assesses the cleaning ability of both smooth and interproximal surfaces, and the single half cylinder model (SHC model), which measures the following ability of the toothbrush bristles on convex surfaces. Two types of test toothbrushes were used: small toothbrush with simple structure (toothbrush S) and large, functionally designed toothbrush (toothbrush G). Statistical analyses were performed using t‑tests and Bonferroni correction was applied when multiple comparisons were performed. The results indicated that toothbrush G had equal or greater cleaning ability than toothbrush S across all tested angles in the smooth and interproximal surface model. The minimum following load necessary for effective cleaning without bristle bounce was significantly lower (p = 0.01) for toothbrush G (1.25 N) than for toothbrush S (3.84 N), suggesting that toothbrush G is less dependent on brushing technique and more suitable for a wide range of individuals, regardless of their brushing skills. In this study, we confirmed that it is possible to significantly detect differences in toothbrush functionality (cleaning and following ability of toothbrush) by using two in vitro models of partial tooth-surface. Continued development of these models can potentially contribute to the standardization of toothbrush evaluation.

item.title: Geographic and Socioeconomic Disparities in Stage at Diagnosis and Nodal Burden Among Patients With HPV-Era Oropharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma in Louisiana: A Population-Based Analysis.
item.dc:creator: Schaefer J, Son L, Fang Z, Walvekar RR
item.description:
Authors: Schaefer J, Son L, Fang Z, Walvekar RR
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70562
Published: 2026-Nov-24
PMID: 43076213



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stage at diagnosis is a strong predictor of survival in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC). Gulf South population-level data on these disparities remain limited. METHODS: We analyzed 1344 patients with known stage at diagnosis from Louisiana Tumor Registry data (n = 1698 cases, 2018-2023). Geographic access was operationalized as straight-line distance from parish centroid to the nearest academic medical center (AMC), categorized as < 25, 25-50, and > 50 miles. Multivariable logistic regression examined predictors of advanced-stage presentation (Stage III-IV) and nodal burden (N2-N3). RESULTS: Advanced-stage disease increased with distance from AMC (33.8%, 38.7%, 46.6%; Mantel-Haenszel χ2 = 13.4, p = 0.0003). Distance > 50 miles independently predicted advanced-stage presentation (OR 1.56, p = 0.008) and high nodal burden (OR 1.44, p = 0.030). Black race (OR 2.25), Medicaid (OR 1.62), and smoking (OR 2.91) were independent predictors. HPV-positive histology was strongly protective (OR 0.33, p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Distance from specialty care independently predicts advanced-stage OPSCC and extensive nodal disease even after controlling for HPV status, race, insurance, and socioeconomic factors, supporting targeted teleoncology expansion and rural outreach initiatives.

item.title: Blinded Evaluation of Patient-Facing Thyroid Cancer Information From Clinicians, Large Language Models, and Web Search.
item.dc:creator: Hack S, Karni RJ, Coblens O, Hayu D, Sonnino R, Minkowitz G, Krinsky D, Locatello LG, Malkin BD, Rivero A, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Hack S, Karni RJ, Coblens O, Hayu D, Sonnino R, Minkowitz G, Krinsky D, Locatello LG, Malkin BD, Rivero A, et al.
Journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1002/ohn.70497
Published: 2026-Nov-24
PMID: 43076196



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the quality of patient-facing thyroid cancer information generated by clinicians, large language models (LLMs), and web search results using parallel expert and layperson evaluation under blinded conditions. STUDY DESIGN: Blinded comparative evaluation study. SETTING: Online, text-based assessment of patient-facing health information. METHODS: Thirty commonly searched thyroid cancer questions were identified using Google Trends. For each question, patient-facing answers were generated by a fellowship-trained head and neck surgeon, 5 widely used LLMs (GPT-4, GPT-5, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek), and the first nonsponsored Google search result. Responses were anonymised and source-blinded. Seven attending physicians evaluated responses using the Quality Analysis of Medical AI (QAMAI) framework across 5 domains, and 15 lay participants evaluated the same responses across 4 patient-centred domains. Ratings were analysed at the question level using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), Friedman tests, Kendall's W, and post-hoc Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. RESULTS: Expert inter-rater reliability was good across domains (ICC 0.78-0.82). Expert ratings differed significantly across sources (P < .001; Kendall's W = 0.70-0.81), with Claude achieving the highest expert scores and Google-derived responses the lowest. Layperson ratings also differed significantly (P < .001; Kendall's W = 0.70-0.87) but clustered near the upper end of the scale, indicating a ceiling effect. The largest expert-rated differences occurred for treatment-related questions, particularly radioactive iodine therapy. CONCLUSION: Patient-facing thyroid cancer information quality varies across clinicians, LLMs, and web search results. Divergence between expert and layperson assessments indicates that perceived clarity and reassurance do not reliably reflect expert-defined completeness or clinical robustness.

item.title: Nasal Septal Perforation Due to Cryoglobulinemic Vasculitis: A Case Report.
item.dc:creator: Lin EY, Zhou AS, Grey S
item.description:
Authors: Lin EY, Zhou AS, Grey S
Journal: The Annals of otology, rhinology, and laryngology | DOI: 10.1177/00034894261511058
Published: 2026-Nov-24
PMID: 43075940



Abstract:
Nasal septal perforation (NSP) is a known complication of nasal trauma such as surgery or cauterization, intranasal drug use, autoinflammatory or autoimmune conditions, and infection. Cryoglobulinemic vasculitis (CV) is a less common cause of NSP in which immune complexes precipitate in and occlude small vessels, leading to ischemic necrosis of the nasal septal mucosa. This is a case report of a 75-year-old female patient with monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) and associated type I CV who presented with longstanding, recurrent bilateral nasal crusting, and was found to have a large anterior NSP with normal-appearing margins. Given her otherwise unremarkable medical or social history, her presentation was most likely attributable to the known CV. Biopsy to rule out malignancy was deferred, and it was anticipated that there would significant improvement in sinonasal symptoms with treatment of the underlying conditions. Therefore, the patient was initiated on low dose prednisone with subsequent taper, in addition to pre-existing plasma cell-directed therapy and dexamethasone, and the nasal crusting and drainage significantly improved after 2 weeks without need for surgical intervention.

item.title: Pneumocephalus After Positive Pressure Ventilation Without Skull Base Defect: A Diagnostic Quest.
item.dc:creator: Kajal S, Chopra P, Bajaj D, Gandicheruvu H, Halawi A, Kazemizadeh Gol MA, Ashley W
item.description:
Authors: Kajal S, Chopra P, Bajaj D, Gandicheruvu H, Halawi A, Kazemizadeh Gol MA, Ashley W
Journal: The Annals of otology, rhinology, and laryngology | DOI: 10.1177/00034894261510589
Published: 2026-Nov-24
PMID: 43075931



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pneumocephalus typically results from craniofacial trauma, tumors, infections, or skull base defects. Acute pneumocephalus in a patient without prior neurological history or obvious skull base defects presents a diagnostic challenge. CASE PRESENTATION: A 65-year-old male with a history of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma and multiple esophageal dilations post-radiation presented with hypercapnic respiratory failure. He developed acute-onset altered mental status after initiation of Bilevel Positive Airway Pressure (BiPAP). An urgent head computed tomography (CT) scan showed pneumocephalus, and subsequent sinus CTs showed no skull base defects. Nasal endoscopy showed no obvious clear fluid drainage, and nasal secretions tested negative for beta-2 transferrin. Retrospective review of a chest CT from 3 months prior revealed a small proximal esophageal defect with prevertebral air tracking. Follow-up CT imaging confirmed air tracking along the T1 costovertebral joint, identifying an enterothecal fistula as the route for positive-pressure air entry into the spinal canal and cranial vault. The pneumocephalus resolved within 10 days with conservative measures. Although surgical obliteration of the fistula was discussed, the patient opted against surgical intervention. CONCLUSION: Spontaneous or positive-pressure-induced pneumocephalus without a skull base defect should prompt investigation of alternative air-entry pathways, including enterothecal fistulas, particularly in patients with predisposing risk factors such as esophageal malignancy and dilations.

item.title: Feasibility of Implementing Prehabilitation and Enhanced Recovery After Surgery in a Head and Neck Surgical Cohort With Free Flap Reconstruction.
item.dc:creator: Service CA, Jones ACM, Anderson B, Chia PH, D'Souza AN, Davies LM, Di Luca B, Hoogenhout L, Koehl EM, Leslie E, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Service CA, Jones ACM, Anderson B, Chia PH, D'Souza AN, Davies LM, Di Luca B, Hoogenhout L, Koehl EM, Leslie E, et al.
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70554
Published: 2026-Nov-24
PMID: 43075817



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Royal Melbourne Hospital implemented an Enhanced Recovery After Surgery program with prehabilitation (ERAS+) for patients undergoing head and neck (HN) surgery with free flap (FF) reconstruction. This study evaluated the feasibility of ERAS+. METHODS: Feasibility was assessed using Bowen's Framework in patients undergoing HN surgery with FF reconstruction between May 2023 and August 2024. Clinical outcomes were compared with a historical cohort treated before ERAS+ implementation (January 2022 to January 2023). RESULTS: ERAS+ achieved high prehabilitation uptake (91%) and attendance (90%). Patient satisfaction was high (90%-96%), and compliance with ERAS protocols improved by 22.1%. Median hospital length of stay was 2 days shorter within the ERAS+ cohort (15 vs. 17 days; p = 0.115). Postoperative complications, return to surgery, readmission, time to decannulation, time to oral intake and 28-day survival were similar between groups. CONCLUSIONS: ERAS+ implementation was feasible and improved perioperative pathway compliance, with no clear impact on length of stay or complication rates.

item.title: Periostin in Pediatric Adenoid Hypertrophy.
item.dc:creator: Degirmenci N, Ozdem A, Firat CK, Yakut K, Aksoy T, Ozturan O
item.description:
Authors: Degirmenci N, Ozdem A, Firat CK, Yakut K, Aksoy T, Ozturan O
Journal: The Annals of otology, rhinology, and laryngology | DOI: 10.1177/00034894261508742
Published: 2026-Nov-23
PMID: 43074183



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Periostin is a matricellular protein implicated in structural tissue changes and chronic inflammation. Adenoid hypertrophy (AH) is thought to be driven by chronic inflammatory stimulation, in which recurrent antigen exposure promotes lymphoid hyperplasia and persistent enlargement of adenoid tissue. However, the molecular mediators contributing to adenoid tissue remodeling remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to evaluate serum and tissue periostin levels in children with AH. METHODS: This prospective controlled study included children aged 2 to 8 years. The study group consisted of children with grade 3 to 4 AH scheduled for adenoidectomy, while the control group comprised children with grade 1 AH without clinically significant disease. Serum and tissue periostin levels were compared. RESULTS: Serum periostin levels were significantly higher in children with AH compared with controls (P = .019). In addition, periostin concentrations were significantly increased in adenoid tissue compared with paired normal nasopharyngeal mucosal tissue (P = .016). CONCLUSION: The findings of this study demonstrate that periostin levels are elevated both systemically and locally in children with AH. This elevation suggests that periostin-associated inflammatory and remodeling pathways may play a role in the pathophysiology of AH. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT04152746.

item.title: Sustaining rural cultural memory through oral history: A case study of spatial reconstruction in a demolished village.
item.dc:creator: Zhang T, Ding C, Cheng X, Yang C, Zheng D, Chen K
item.description:
Authors: Zhang T, Ding C, Cheng X, Yang C, Zheng D, Chen K
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0362355
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43071660



Abstract:
Rapid urbanization and large-scale village demolition in China have erased many traditional rural settlements from the physical landscape, but not from residents' memories. How to reconstruct these invisible spaces and sustain local culture in the absence of material fabric remains an underexplored question in rural sustainability research. This qualitative case study focuses on Shixinzhuang, a demolished village now occupied by the new campus of Zhengzhou University in central China. We conducted in-depth oral history interviews with six long-term residents selected through purposive sampling based on native attachment, spatial role, and generational span. During interviews, participants drew cognitive maps starting from their own courtyards to locate streets, public facilities, production zones, and ritual spaces. Hand-drawn maps were systematically organized and compared to identify shared spatial patterns and memory discrepancies. This information was further cross-verified through data triangulation with archival photographs, satellite imagery, field revisits, and focused validation discussions. Data analysis centered on themes of spatial memory, memory places, and cultural sustainability. Findings indicate that despite the complete demolition of the physical village, Shixinzhuang's spatial structure can still be systematically reconstructed from villagers' memories. Residents consistently recalled the village's evolution from a walled enclosure to an open, expanding settlement. Its spatial organization was structured around a "cross-street" skeleton formed by a north-south main street and an east-west auxiliary street, with housing in the central area growing organically while peripheral housing was more orderly. Spatial memories were highly clustered around several "memory places," notably the Nainai Miao (Grandmother Temple), ancestral grave areas, and residential rooftop platforms. Even after relocation, these places continue to carry kinship ties, religious rituals, and neighborhood interactions. Furthermore, production spaces reflected layered institutional experiences transitioning from collective agriculture to a marginal industrial belt, with distinct intergenerational differences emerging in narratives differentiating between "collective labor" and "earning money in the brick kilns." Ultimately, the joint process of narration, mapping, and iterative correction transformed the oral history practice from a unidirectional recording into a reflexive, participatory act of "re-creating place." This study demonstrates that even when a traditional village has disappeared from the ground, its spatial structure and symbolic places can be recovered through the combined use of oral history and cognitive mapping, and mobilized as resources for rural cultural sustainability. For demolished settlements, integrating narrative-based spatial reconstruction into planning, heritage management, and community-building can help re-anchor local identity, inform commemorative and interpretive design, and institutionalize residents' narrative participation in rural spatial governance.

item.title: Multitarget docking and toxicity-guided prioritisation of phytochemicals from Bangladeshi medicinal plants against wheat fungal pathogens.
item.dc:creator: Ope MS, Ashrafuzzaman M
item.description:
Authors: Ope MS, Ashrafuzzaman M
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0356864
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43071659



Abstract:
The rising issue of fungicide resistance, along with environmental concerns related to synthetic fungicides, highlights the need for safer and more sustainable antifungal agents. In this computational study, we screened nineteen phytochemicals from locally available medicinal plants in Bangladesh against three fungal protein targets associated with major wheat diseases: class I sesquiterpene synthase (PDB ID: 8H4P) and trichothecene 3-O-acetyltransferase (TRI101; PDB ID: 3B2S) from Fusarium graminearum, and the AvrSr50 effector protein (PDB ID: 7MQQ) from Puccinia graminis f. sp. tritici. Blind docking was performed using AutoDock Vina (with an exhaustiveness setting of 16) and evaluated for reliability through consensus docking with CB-Dock2. We analyzed protein-ligand interactions using BIOVIA Discovery Studio, and the top-ranked compounds were further assessed for toxicity and ADMET (Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity) properties with ProTox-3 and ADMETlab 3.0. Thevetin B, Thevetin A, and Uscharin were computationally prioritized as candidate multitarget binders. Notably, Thevetin B formed extensive hydrogen-bond and hydrophobic interaction networks across all three proteins and showed comparatively strong predicted binding affinities. However, ProTox-3 predicted high acute oral toxicity for Thevetin B (LD₅₀ = 4 mg/kg, Class I) and Thevetin A (LD₅₀ = 8 mg/kg, Class II), while Uscharin had a substantially higher predicted LD₅₀ (2000 mg/kg, Class IV). The ADMET analysis revealed shared liabilities such as mutagenicity and nephrotoxicity, along with limited absorption, but also highlighted compound-specific differences in physicochemical properties and environmental toxicity. These findings indicate an efficacy-safety trade-off among the computationally prioritized candidates and support their further evaluation as testable hypotheses rather than establishing a definitive efficacy-safety hierarchy. This study provides a structured computational prioritization of locally available phytochemicals and emphasizes that any claims of practical antifungal utility must be supported by experimental validation of both efficacy and safety.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Risk stratification systems are essential for individualized management of differentiated thyroid cancer. This study compared the 2015 and 2025 American Thyroid Association (ATA) guidelines in predicting long-term recurrence risk in patients with papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC). METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 2677 adult patients with PTC who underwent total thyroidectomy at a tertiary academic center between 2010 and 2015. Patients were stratified according to the 2015 and 2025 ATA guidelines. The primary outcome was structural persistent or recurrent disease (clinical event). RESULTS: Risk distribution differed significantly between the two systems, with 526 patients (19.6%) upstaged under the 2025 ATA guidelines. Compared with the 2015 ATA system, the 2025 ATA system assigned fewer patients to the low-risk group (27.8% vs. 15.1%) and more to the high-risk group (9.9% vs. 16.8%). By the 2015 ATA, 1668 patients (62.3%) were classified as intermediate-risk. By the 2025 ATA, 882 (32.9%) and 940 patients (35.1%) were classified as low-intermediate- and intermediate-high-risk, respectively. Over a median follow-up of 9.6 years (interquartile range: 6.6-12.2 years), 132 (4.9%) patients experienced clinical events. Event rates among low-risk patients were 1.2% under the 2015 ATA system and 0.7% under the 2025 ATA system. Among intermediate-risk patients, the event rate was 4.4% with the 2015 ATA guidelines, compared with 0.9% and 5.3% in the low-intermediate and intermediate-high groups, respectively, under the 2025 ATA system. Among high-risk patients, event rates were 18.5% and 15.7% under the 2015 and 2025 ATA systems, respectively. Harrell's C-index was 0.711 ([confidence interval or CI, 0.672-0.750]) for the 2015 ATA classification and 0.781 ([CI, 0.748-0.814]) for the 2025 ATA classification, with a difference of 0.069 ([CI, 0.042-0.097]; p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: The 2025 ATA risk stratification system was more granular, showed improved discrimination, and more precisely identified patients at very low risk of recurrence. However, a substantial proportion of patients were reclassified into higher-risk categories, which may have implications for potential overtreatment and warrants careful consideration.

item.title: Long-Term Nonmalignant Chronic Health Conditions in Childhood, Adolescent, and Young Adult Differentiated Thyroid Carcinoma Survivors and the Impact of Radioactive Iodine Therapy: Evidence from Real-World Data.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Differentiated thyroid carcinoma (DTC) is the most common endocrine malignancy in children, adolescents, and young adults (CAYA) with survival exceeding 98%. Real-world data on long-term nonmalignant chronic health conditions (CHCs) remain scarce. OBJECTIVE: To characterize long-term nonmalignant CHCs in CAYA DTC survivors relative to cancer-free controls and explore associations with radioactive iodine (RAI) exposure. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used Clalit Health Services electronic health records (Israel, 1982-2022) comparing 5267 DTC survivors (diagnosed at age < 40) with 21,062 matched cancer-free controls. Incident CHCs occurring ≥2 years post-DTC diagnosis/index-date were assessed across metabolic, cardiovascular, renal, hepatic, gastrointestinal, pulmonary, skeletal, autoimmune/rheumatologic, and emotional domains and were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RAI subgroup analyses were exploratory. RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 14.7 years (interquartile range 8.8-23.2), the risk of developing ≥1 CHC did not differ significantly between DTC survivors and cancer-free controls (54.4% vs. 52.0%; HR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.00-1.11; p = 0.066). Survivors were more likely to experience multimorbidity (≥2 CHCs 35.7% vs. 32.0%) and had higher risks of several specific organ-system conditions: osteoporosis (HR 1.33; 95% CI: 1.14-1.56), chronic kidney disease (HR 1.61; 95% CI: 1.32-1.96), gastroesophageal disorders (HR 1.35; 95% CI: 1.26-1.45), dyslipidemia (HR 1.23; 95% CI: 1.16-1.32), and hypertension (HR 1.21; 95% CI: 1.13-1.29). Pulmonary, cardiovascular, autoimmune, hepatic, and clinically diagnosed emotional disorders did not differ significantly between groups. Exploratory analyses revealed a dose-dependent RAI risk gradient (1 course: HR 1.20; 95% CI: 1.06-1.35; ≥2 courses: HR 1.33; 95% CI: 1.16-1.52). CONCLUSIONS: Despite excellent overall survival, CAYA DTC survivors face a modest overall increase in CHC risk alongside notably greater multisystem morbidity. RAI-associated risk trends are exploratory and need further research. These findings support risk-adapted therapy and structured long-term survivorship monitoring.

Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Free flap reconstruction has become the gold standard after major oncologic resections in the head and neck (HN) region. Despite advances in techniques, free flaps undergo volumetric and structural changes over time, potentially compromising functional and aesthetic outcomes. This study aims to explore a solid three-dimensional method to perform multiparametric assessment of free flaps. METHODS AND MATERIALS: A cohort of 32 patients undergoing ablative HN surgery followed by free flap reconstruction was studied, using postoperative CT/MRI scans at fixed intervals. Semi-automatic 3D segmentation was adopted to measure soft tissue flap parameters, excluding bone. Both cross-sectional and longitudinal analyses examined dimensional changes, separating fasciocutaneous and muscular components. RESULTS: Cross-sectional analysis showed significant dimensional variability among anatomical subsites, particularly in the volume and thickness of fasciocutaneous components. Longitudinal data revealed that muscular flap components underwent significantly greater reductions in diameter, surface area, and volume compared to fasciocutaneous tissue, which remained relatively stable over time. No significant differences in dimensional changes were observed between different flap types overtime. CONCLUSION: This study presents a reproducible 3D methodology for multiparametric assessment of free flaps in HN reconstruction. The marked reduction in muscular components relative to fasciocutaneous tissues highlights the importance of considering differential shrinkage in surgical planning and potential overcorrection. Future prospective studies with larger cohorts and earlier imaging are needed to validate and optimize reconstructive strategies.

item.title: CBCT-based radiomics of the crista galli: association with an exploratory composite anatomical complexity framework in a preliminary study.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the association between CBCT-based radiomic features of the crista galli (CG) and anterior skull base anatomical complexity using the exploratory Anatomical Complexity Score (ACS). METHODS: This retrospective exploratory pilot study included 50 CBCT images. CG anatomy was evaluated using the Keros, Komut-Golpinar, Hajiioannou, and pneumatization classifications and integrated into the exploratory ACS framework. Following three-dimensional segmentation, 107 radiomic features were extracted. Associations between radiomic features and ACS were analyzed, and exploratory linear and logistic regression models were developed. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. RESULTS: Thirty participants (60.0%) were classified as low complexity and 20 (40.0%) as moderate complexity; no high-complexity cases were identified. Among the four constituent classifications, Keros showed the largest internal association with the composite ACS (p < 0.001, ε² = 0.372). Several radiomic features showed nominal correlations with continuous ACS and unadjusted differences between ACS-based groups. None of the correlations with continuous ACS remained statistically significant after FDR correction; subsequent ROC and modeling analyses were treated as exploratory. In exploratory ROC analyses based on features identified in the unadjusted analyses, GLSZM Size Zone Non-Uniformity demonstrated the highest moderate discriminative performance for differentiating low- and moderate-complexity groups (AUC = 0.743), followed by GLDM Dependence Non-Uniformity (AUC = 0.733) and GLCM Cluster Prominence (AUC = 0.718). The exploratory radiomics-only logistic regression model demonstrated an apparent AUC of 0.743, while 5-fold cross-validation yielded a mean AUC of 0.715. CONCLUSIONS: CBCT-based radiomic features of the CG showed exploratory associations with ACS. However, none of the correlations with continuous ACS remained statistically significant after FDR correction. The proposed ACS framework should therefore be regarded as a preliminary exploratory tool rather than a validated clinical outcome-prediction tool. Further validation in larger independent cohorts is required before any clinical application.

item.title: Surgical margins in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma: A European Head and Neck Society (EHNS) multidisciplinary modified Delphi consensus.

item.description:

Published: 2026-Nov-22

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgical margin assessment in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) remains poorly standardized by HPV status, subsite, and treatment context. This European Head and Neck Society (EHNS) consensus aimed to harmonize margin assessment and margin-based decisions. METHODS: Following systematic review, 25 multidisciplinary panelists evaluated recommendations through two Delphi rounds; consensus was ≥80 % and near-consensus 70-79.9 %. Margindefinitionswerebasedonformalin-fixed,paraffin-embeddedsections,notintraoperativeor postoperativegrossingestimates. RESULTS: Of 48 recommendations, 32 reached consensus, six near-consensus, and 10 were rejected. "Ink on tumor" defined a positive margin irrespective of HPV status (96 %). A 5-mm mucosal margin was retained for HPV-negative OPSCC (84 %), whereas 3 mm reached near-consensus for HPV-positive disease (78.3 %); smaller thresholds were unsupported. A clear margin alone should not determine adjuvant treatment (78.3 %, near-consensus). Re-resection was recommended when the margin site was identifiable and would change adjuvant management. Positive margins warranted radiotherapy in pT1-T2 HPV-positive disease without other adverse features (80 %), whereas chemoradiotherapy was recommended with high-risk features, such as pT3-T4 disease or extranodal extension (95.8 %), and in HPV-negative disease (100 %). For close margins, selective de-escalation could be considered in highly selected HPV-positive disease without high-risk features (82.6 %), whereas HPV-negative disease warranted radiotherapy, with escalation according to additional risks (91.3 %). In fit patients aged ≥70 years with positive margins, radiotherapy alone was favored for HPV-positive disease (87.5 %), while chemoradiotherapy was retained for fit patients with HPV-negative disease (95.7 %). CONCLUSIONS: This consensus provides a multidisciplinary framework for harmonized OPSCC margin assessment and risk-adapted postoperative management across HPV status, anatomy, and treatment-related morbidity.

item.description:
Authors: Chen S, Evans LK, Lin ME, Sayeed S, St John MA, Han PS, Chhetri DK
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71021
Published: 2026-Nov-22

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluates human papillomavirus (HPV) knowledge and vaccine receptiveness among patients at an otolaryngology clinic in a county hospital setting. METHODS: Surveys were provided to adult patients between September 2023 and July 2026. Surveys were offered in English and Spanish and assessed awareness of HPV, knowledge of association with cervical and oropharyngeal cancers, and willingness to undergo HPV vaccination. Demographic data including sex, age, race/ethnicity, vaccination status, and HPV-related disease were also collected. Chi-squared and Fisher's exact test compared differences between males and females. RESULTS: Two hundred and one patients completed the questionnaire with demographic data available in 86. Most were Spanish-speaking, female, Hispanic, and not vaccinated against HPV. 52.2% (105/201) had heard of HPV while 25.1% (50/199) knew HPV could cause oropharyngeal cancer. Almost three-fifths had not heard of the HPV vaccine (60.2%, 121/201), but if offered, 33.0% (64/194) were open to receiving it. Compared with males, females were statistically more likely to have heard of HPV, understand its association with cervical and oropharyngeal cancer, and believe in the HPV vaccine's efficacy. There were no statistical differences by sex in willingness to receive the vaccine, if offered. CONCLUSION: There is low HPV health literacy and vaccination rates among this county otolaryngology clinic population. Despite this, these patients are highly receptive to receiving the vaccine if offered. item.title: Allogeneic umbilical cord-mesenchymal stem/stromal cells for chronic radiation-induced xerostomia: a phase I study with multimodal functional and imaging assessment.

Published: 2026-Nov-21

Abstract:
PURPOSE: Radiation-induced xerostomia is a clinically significant adverse effect of head and neck radiotherapy with limited treatment options. This prospective, single-arm case series evaluated the safety, feasibility, and exploratory clinical efficacy of ultrasound-guided intraglandular administration of allogeneic umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (UC-MSCs) in patients with chronic radiation-induced xerostomia. METHODS AND MATERIALS: Ten disease-free survivors of oropharyngeal cancer with CTCAE grade 2-3 xerostomia received ultrasound-guided UC-MSC injections into both parotid and submandibular glands. Each parotid gland received 50 × 10⁶ UC-MSCs and each submandibular gland 25 × 10⁶ UC-MSCs. Safety was the primary outcome. Exploratory assessments were performed at baseline and at 1 and 4 months and included patient-reported outcome measures, unstimulated and stimulated salivary flow rates, salivary biochemical analyses, magnetic resonance imaging, ultrasound shear-wave elastography, salivary gland scintigraphy, and, where feasible, core-needle biopsy. RESULTS: No serious adverse events were observed. Procedure-related effects were limited to transient injection-site pain, swelling, and local discomfort. Objective salivary flow rates and most biochemical parameters remained stable throughout follow-up. In contrast, patient-reported outcomes improved, with the greatest changes at 4 months. Xerostomia Questionnaire scores decreased from 63.44 ± 16.81 at baseline to 53.18 ± 21.16 at 4 months (p = 0.0066), and visual analogue scale scores from 64.65 ± 17.30 to 60.29 ± 18.11 (p = 0.0122). Improvements were also observed in xerostomia and sticky saliva domains of the EORTC QLQ-H&N35. MRI showed only subtle changes in T2-weighted signal intensity ratios, while elastography remained unchanged. Scintigraphy demonstrated increased excretion velocity at 4 months (p = 0.0355). CONCLUSIONS: In this single-arm case series of 10 patients, ultrasound-guided intraglandular UC-MSC administration was feasible and well tolerated over four months, with no serious adverse events. Improvements in PROMs and scintigraphic excretion velocity were exploratory findings in the absence of a control group and occurred despite largely unchanged salivary flow. Clinical efficacy remains to be established in adequately powered, randomized, placebo-controlled trials.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Our objectives were to determine the association between high peri-tumoral immune infiltrate (PTII) and survival, determine the association between cancer associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and PTII and to characterize immune cell density at the invasive front of oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC). Abstract:
PURPOSE: Eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis (ECRS), a type 2-dominant form of chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps, is characterized by frequent postoperative relapse. Although statins exhibit pleiotropic anti-inflammatory and profibrinolytic properties that may mitigate impaired fibrinolysis in ECRS, their clinical impact remains unclear. This study evaluated the association between statin use and postoperative recurrence in patients with ECRS undergoing functional endoscopic sinus surgery (FESS). METHODS: This single-center, retrospective, observational study included patients diagnosed with ECRS according to the Japanese Epidemiological Survey of Refractory Eosinophilic Chronic Rhinosinusitis criteria who underwent FESS between April 2015 and December 2025. Postoperative recurrence was defined as the need for any of the following treatment escalations: revision surgery, systemic oral corticosteroid therapy, local triamcinolone administration, or use of (or eligibility for) biologic therapy. RESULTS: Forty-nine patients completed at least 6 months of follow-up, including 11 statin users (22.4%). Statin users were significantly older than non-users (60.9 vs. 52.3 years; p=0.033), whereas other baseline characteristics were comparable. Statin use was associated with lower odds of overall postoperative recurrence (27.3% vs. 63.2%; OR 0.22; 95% CI 0.05-0.96; p=0.046). CONCLUSION: Statin use was associated with lower odds of overall postoperative recurrence in patients with ECRS. However, this association was attenuated after adjustment for age and asthma and should be considered hypothesis-generating. Larger prospective multicenter studies are needed to confirm these findings.

Abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the prognostic significance of pretreatment gross tumor volume (GTV) and determine whether volumetric assessment provides additional prognostic value beyond conventional TNM staging in patients with locally advanced laryngeal and hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma treated with definitive radiotherapy, predominantly with concurrent systemic therapy. METHODS: This retrospective study included 124 patients treated with definitive radiotherapy between 2012 and 2024; 117 received concurrent systemic therapy. Pretreatment GTVprimary, GTVnodal, and GTVtotal were measured on planning CT for patients treated with upfront radiotherapy and on the CT component of pre-induction PET/CT for patients receiving induction chemotherapy. Receiver operating characteristic analysis was used to determine cutoff values. Survival outcomes were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses. The incremental prognostic value of volumetric parameters was assessed using Akaike's Information Criterion (AIC)-based model comparison. RESULTS: The selected cutoff value for GTVtotal was 36 cc. Although GTVprimary showed the highest AUC in ROC analysis, GTVtotal remained associated with disease-specific survival after multivariable adjustment and yielded the lowest AIC among the compared models. item.title: Sentinel lymph node biopsy using ICG-[99mTc]Tc-nanocolloid and superselective level I dissection.

Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) is a widely used diagnostic procedure for early-stage oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC) in Europe. However, earlier studies used only radioactive tracers. European guidelines now recommend combining a fluorescent tracer with superselective neck dissection (SSND) of level I for FOMSCC. Staging included ultrasound, with fine needle aspiration for suspicious nodes, and CT or MRI as indicated. SLNB was performed using ICG-[99mTc]Tc-nanocolloid, planar lymphoscintigraphy, and SPECT/CT. Abstract:
PURPOSE: To characterize the clinicopathological features and long-term outcomes of minor salivary gland tumors and evaluate stage migration and survival stratification after restaging malignant tumors according to the American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) version 9. All tumors underwent descriptive analysis; malignancies were restaged under the AJCC eighth edition and Version 9 and analyzed for survival. Median follow-up for malignant cases was 109 months; 5-year OS, RFS, and DSS were 69.1%, 85.0%, and 77.7%, respectively. Version 9 significantly stratified OS and DSS (p = 0.024 and p = 0.028), whereas the eighth-edition grouping did not (p = 0.075 and p = 0.176); neither system stratified RFS. Nodal involvement was associated with poorer OS and DSS (both p < 0.001), perineural invasion with poorer OS (p = 0.031), and positive margins with poorer RFS (p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: AJCC Version 9 produced clinically relevant T-category migration and significantly stratified OS and DSS in this cohort. In univariable analyses, nodal involvement was associated with poorer OS and DSS, perineural invasion with poorer OS, and positive surgical margins with poorer RFS. Larger studies using complete stage groups and formal model-performance measures are needed to confirm these findings.

Abstract:
PURPOSE: Salivary gland cancers (SGC) are rare and heterogeneous, exhibiting markedly diverse biological behavior and clinical courses. This, together with their generally poor response rates to systemic chemotherapy, has driven research into specific and/or recurrent genetic alterations that may have diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic relevance. This review provides an overview of current knowledge concerning the molecular basis of SGC. METHODS: A comprehensive review of the literature from the last 15 years was performed, focusing on molecular alterations and targeted therapeutic approaches in the following salivary gland carcinomas: salivary duct carcinoma (SDC), myoepithelial carcinoma (MECA), polymorphous adenocarcinoma (PAC), carcinoma ex-pleomorphic adenoma (CXPA), and other more rare histological subtypes. RESULTS: Current insights into the clinical and pathogenetic significance of genetic alterations in SGC are presented, their diagnostic and prognostic relevance is discussed, and available targeted therapies are reviewed. SDC is characterized by overexpression of the androgen receptor (AR) in nearly all cases and is HER2 positive in up to 50% of the cases; targeted therapies directed against both AR and HER2 are available. MECA is a fusion-positive cancer, frequently with fusion​s involving PLAG1, while in PAC, molecular alterations typically involve the PRKD genes. However, targeted treatments are still lacking for both entities. CXPA should be treated according to the specific subtype. CONCLUSION: A deeper understanding of the molecular pathogenesis of SGCs may enable refined diagnosis, more precise definition of prognostic subtypes, and identification of tumor-specific targets for personalized therapies.

item.title: GLP-1 receptor agonists in idiopathic subglottic stenosis: patient attitudes, barriers, facilitators and patient-reported outcomes.
item.dc:creator: Gosselin LE, Anderson C, Al Yaghchi C
item.description:
Authors: Gosselin LE, Anderson C, Al Yaghchi C
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10835-3
Published: 2026-Nov-21
PMID: 43066751



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Idiopathic subglottic stenosis (iSGS) is a rare disease of unknown etiology. There has been a growing interest within the patient community regarding the potential therapeutic role of GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RA) in the management of iSGS, potentially through weight loss-mediated or direct anti-inflammatory mechanisms. The objective of this study was to evaluate patient perspectives and attitudes regarding the potential role of GLP-1 RA in the overall management of iSGS. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional observational study through a structured online anonymous survey. The survey comprised 53 items organized across four domains: demographics; attitudes, barriers and facilitators to GLP-1 RA use; therapy details and adverse effects; and perceived therapeutic impact. RESULTS: A total of 1382 patients with iSGS completed the survey. Diagnostic delay of iSGS was a prominent finding, with patients reporting a substantial lag between symptom onset and confirmed diagnosis. Overall, 407 patients used GLP-1 RA therapy. Among GLP-1 RA users, 38.44% self-reported perceived improvement in airway symptoms. Key barriers to GLP-1 RA therapy included cost, access, and limited physician awareness. Thematic analysis of the patient's responses revealed patients' attitudes toward GLP-1 RA therapy were largely favorable, with patients citing anti-inflammatory benefits and quality of life improvements as primary motivators for use. CONCLUSION: GLP-1 receptor agonists are generally viewed favorably by patients with iSGS. Patient-reported experiences suggest possible improvements in airway symptoms, although prospective studies are required to establish causality and clarify mechanistic benefit.

item.title: Network meta-analysis of induction chemotherapy combined with concurrent chemoradiotherapy and immunotherapy in advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Zeng J, Qiu L, Zhou Y, Zeng Y, Wang Y, Li J
item.description:
Authors: Zeng J, Qiu L, Zhou Y, Zeng Y, Wang Y, Li J
Journal: American journal of otolaryngology | DOI: 10.1016/j.amjoto.2026.104995
Published: 2026-Nov-20
PMID: 43072315



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) carries high risks of distant and locoregional recurrence. Induction chemotherapy (IC) with concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) is being investigated; optimal strategies remain undefined. This network meta-analysis aimed to evaluate and rank various IC and ICI-integrated regimens in advanced NPC. METHODS: This network meta-analysis was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261278226). PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched until July 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating IC and/or ICIs with CCRT in advanced NPC were included. Outcomes included overall survival (OS), distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS), and locoregional recurrence-free survival (LRFS). Network meta-analyses were performed using a frequentist framework. Risk of bias and evidence certainty were assessed using Cochrane RoB 2.0 and GRADE, respectively. RESULTS: Fifteen RCTs involving 5160 patients and 14 regimens were included. For OS, docetaxel plus cisplatin (TP) + CCRT showed a favorable treatment effect compared with CCRT alone (HR = 0.21, 95% CI: 0.09-0.50; SUCRA = 86.4%), although its ranking remained uncertain in sensitivity analysis (probability of ranking first: 46.7%). For DMFS, gemcitabine plus cisplatin (GP) + CCRT with concurrent and adjuvant camrelizumab (HR = 0.23, 95% CI: 0.11-0.49; SUCRA = 86.4%), adjuvant camrelizumab (HR = 0.23, 95% CI: 0.10-0.51; SUCRA = 86.1%), and induction, concurrent, and adjuvant sintilimab (HR = 0.25, 95% CI: 0.11-0.53; SUCRA = 84.0%) showed favorable results. For LRFS, paclitaxel/cisplatin/capecitabine (TPC) + CCRT (HR = 0.30, 95% CI: 0.11-0.76; SUCRA = 84.8%) and GP + CCRT with concurrent and adjuvant camrelizumab (HR = 0.29, 95% CI: 0.12-0.69; SUCRA = 87.5%) demonstrated favorable treatment effects. No clear evidence of small-study effects was detected, although publication bias could not be definitively excluded. CONCLUSIONS: Integrating IC or anti-programmed cell death protein 1 immunotherapy into CCRT may improve disease control in advanced NPC. Immunotherapy-containing regimens with a GP backbone showed favorable results for preventing distant metastasis, although the relative benefits of different administration sequences and their long-term survival effects remain uncertain. These findings should be interpreted cautiously given the limitations of the evidence network and the available follow-up.

item.title: Clinical-pathological nodal discordance and survival outcomes in oral squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Chang CW, Liao LJ, Hung CY, Cheng PC, Cheng YP, Chiang CJ, Lee WC, Hsu WL, Chen TC
item.description:
Authors: Chang CW, Liao LJ, Hung CY, Cheng PC, Cheng YP, Chiang CJ, Lee WC, Hsu WL, Chen TC
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108233
Published: 2026-Nov-20
PMID: 43063685



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic significance of discordance between clinical and pathological nodal staging in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) remains poorly understood. This study investigates how clinical-pathological nodal discordance impacts survival outcomes in OSCC. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 14,618 OSCC patients from the Taiwan Cancer Registry who underwent primary surgical resection with neck dissection between 2018 and 2022. Patients were stratified into four groups: true negative (cN0pN0), occult metastasis (cN0pN + ), overt metastasis (cN + pN + ), and false positive (cN + pN0). Survival outcomes were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis, propensity score matching, and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. RESULTS: Among 14,618 patients, 7,154 (48.9 %) were true negative, 1,290 (8.8 %) had occult metastasis, 3,197 (21.9 %) had overt metastasis, and 2,977 (20.4 %) were false positive. Approximately 30 % of patients presented with clinical-pathological discordance in neck staging. Despite harboring more advanced T-stage primary tumors, false-positive patients achieved survival outcomes comparable to those of true-negative patients (5-year DFS 71.6 % vs. 71.3 %; OS 76.1 % vs. 75.8 %). Extranodal extension (ENE) was present in 25.5 % of occult metastasis patients and 53.2 % of overt metastasis patients. Regardless of occult or overt presentation, the presence of ENE dictated similarly poor survival outcomes compared with patients without ENE (p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: Clinical-pathological nodal discordance is common in OSCC, and ENE, rather than the clinical detectability of nodal disease, is the dominant prognostic factor in node-positive disease. Elective neck dissection therefore serves a dual diagnostic and therapeutic role, identifying occult metastases that elude preoperative imaging and improving long-term survival.

item.title: Cancer risk with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists: An umbrella review of meta-analyses.
item.dc:creator: Petrelli F, Meregalli G, Berzi D, Nicolì F, Viglino F, Della Pepa G, Indovina F, Dalmiglio C, Forloni F, Bossi A, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Petrelli F, Meregalli G, Berzi D, Nicolì F, Viglino F, Della Pepa G, Indovina F, Dalmiglio C, Forloni F, Bossi A, et al.
Journal: Cancer epidemiology | DOI: 10.1016/j.canep.2026.103273
Published: 2026-Nov-20
PMID: 43063527



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) for diabetes and obesity is increasing, but effects on uncommon or long-latency cancers are uncertain. We synthesised meta-analytic evidence for overall and site-specific cancer risk and assessed methodological quality, overlap, outcome-level certainty, and credibility. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception to 30 June 2026 for meta-analyses of GLP-1RAs or the dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide and incident cancer. Randomised and observational evidence was considered separately; review-level estimates were not recombined. We assessed methodological confidence with AMSTAR 2, overlap with corrected covered area (CCA), outcome-level certainty with a GRADE-informed algorithm, and association credibility with Ioannidis criteria. FINDINGS: We included 38 meta-analyses from 2012 to 2026. The most comprehensive placebo-controlled randomised evidence (48 trials, 94 245 participants, median follow-up 70 weeks) showed no statistically significant association with thyroid cancer (odds ratio [OR] 1·37, 95% CI 0·82-2·31; 1 fewer to 9 more cases per 10 000 treated), pancreatic cancer (0·84, 0·53-1·35), colorectal cancer (1·11, 0·75-1·65), or breast cancer (0·95, 0·60-1·49), and no overall cancer increase (OR 1·05, 0·98-1·13 across 50 trials). Thyroid and agent-specific haematological signals were inconsistent or based on sparse events; between-review discordance for thyroid and colorectal cancer was largely attributable to comparator restriction, choice of estimator, and handling of zero-event trials rather than to differences in cancer ascertainment. Observational syntheses suggested lower hepatocellular carcinoma risk (hazard ratio 0·60, 95% CI 0·41-0·88), but four reviews had very high overlap (CCA 50·0%). Outcome-level certainty was moderate for five outcomes, low for 11, and very low for five; none was high. No association met class I or II credibility criteria. INTERPRETATION: Randomised evidence shows no evidence of a material increase in overall or site-specific cancer risk over currently observed trial durations (median about 70 weeks, maximum about 5 years), and cancer concerns alone do not justify withholding indicated GLP-1RA treatment. Small, rare, long-latency, dose-specific, or agent-specific effects cannot be excluded, and the evidence cannot address exposure beyond approximately five years, well short of the 8-10 years generally required to evaluate cancer incidence. Observational protective associations should not support causal or cancer-prevention claims. FUNDING: None.

item.title: Effects of proton pump inhibitors on serum and fecal biomarkers and intestinal microbiota in dogs.
item.dc:creator: Romano FS, Barbosa IS, Melchert A, Amaral AR, Vendramini THA, Suchodolski J, Lallo MA
item.description:
Authors: Romano FS, Barbosa IS, Melchert A, Amaral AR, Vendramini THA, Suchodolski J, Lallo MA
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361194
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43063192



Abstract:
The gastrointestinal tract of mammals, including dogs and cats, is inhabited by a highly diverse intestinal microbiota that plays an essential role in both health and disease. This microbial ecosystem influences various processes such as metabolism, immunity, neurodevelopment, and the maintenance of homeostasis and can be altered in many circumstances such as diseases, the use of oral medications and gastrointestinal pH. Proton Pump Inhibitors are suspected of causing dysbiosis due to the alteration of gastric pH. This study evaluated the effects PPIs on the microbiota of healthy dogs. Twenty Golden Retrievers were randomly allocated into four treatment groups (n = 5 per group): Omeprazole (OMP - 1 mg/kg twice a day), Esomeprazole (ESO - 1 mg/kg twice a day), Lansoprazole (LSP - 0.5 mg/kg twice a day), and Control (Placebo, CTL) and treated for 30 days. Feces were collected at the beginning (T0) and end (T30) of the trial for evaluation of dysbiosis index and blood biochemistry was performed to quantify target variables of gastrointestinal diseases (folate, cobalamin, iron and calcium) at the same period. Gastrin serum concentrations were evaluated at T0 and T30 only for the LSP group. Results showed no clinical signs or changes in the global dysbiosis index among treatments. However, specific microbial alterations were observed, including a reduction in Turicibacter in the OMP and ESO groups, and an increase in Streptococcus spp. in few individuals in the OMP group. Serum biomarkers related to inflammation and gastrointestinal absorption remained unchanged. In this study, PPIs did not induce intestinal dysbiosis or caused any clinical impairment, although some isolated microbial changes were noted.

item.title: Influence of peri-implant soft tissue thickness on marginal bone loss following immediate implant placement in the anterior maxilla: A retrospective comparative study.
item.dc:creator: Kadkhodazadeh M, Alam M, Golkar M, Naghshbandi T
item.description:
Authors: Kadkhodazadeh M, Alam M, Golkar M, Naghshbandi T
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360723
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43063175



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Marginal bone stability is a critical determinant of the long-term success and esthetic harmony of dental implants. Peri-implant soft tissue thickness (STT) has been proposed as a biological factor influencing crestal bone remodeling. This retrospective comparative study aimed to evaluate the relationship between peri-implant STT and marginal bone loss (MBL) following immediate implant placement in the anterior maxilla after one year of functional loading. METHODS: Fifty immediate implant sites from 50 patients were retrospectively analyzed. Based on mid-buccal soft tissue measurement, implants were classified as thin (STT ≤ 1 mm; n = 22) or thick (STT > 1 mm; n = 28) phenotypes. Clinical parameters, including probing depth, bleeding on probing, plaque index, keratinized tissue width, and pink esthetic score, and radiographic parameters (MBL) were extracted from patient records. MBL was measured on standardized periapical digital radiographs taken immediately after surgery and at one-year follow-up using a custom positioning index. RESULTS: The mean age of participants was 57.88 ± 11.16 years. MBL was significantly higher in the thin soft tissue group (1.34 ± 0.19 mm) compared with the thick tissue group (1.00 ± 0.20 mm; p < 0.0001). STT exhibited a strong negative correlation with MBL (r = -0.749, p < 0.0001). Other variables showed no significant intergroup differences. No significant difference in MBL was observed between implant systems. CONCLUSION: Within the limitations of this retrospective study, peri-implant soft tissue thickness was identified as a key determinant of marginal bone preservation after immediate implant placement in the anterior maxilla. Thicker mucosa was associated with significantly reduced bone resorption and more stable peri-implant esthetic outcomes after one year.

item.title: Induction Immunochemotherapy Followed by Definitive Chemoradiotherapy and Consolidation Immunotherapy for Locally Advanced Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Prospective Phase II Study.
item.dc:creator: Lin L, Li H, Song X, Zhao L, Cheng Y, Liu M, Yu W, Zhang Q, Cai X, Yang Y, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Lin L, Li H, Song X, Zhao L, Cheng Y, Liu M, Yu W, Zhang Q, Cai X, Yang Y, et al.
Journal: International journal of cancer | DOI: 10.1002/ijc.70828
Published: 2026-Nov-19
PMID: 43059192



Abstract:
Long-term survival after definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy (dCCRT) remains limited in locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). We evaluated induction immunochemotherapy followed by dCCRT and consolidation immunotherapy in this setting. This prospective, single-arm Phase II study enrolled 54 adults selected for definitive nonsurgical treatment. The planned regimen comprised two cycles of induction immunochemotherapy with nab-paclitaxel, carboplatin, and a programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) inhibitor, followed by dCCRT with 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions and concurrent weekly chemotherapy. The same PD-1 inhibitor was planned as consolidation therapy for up to 1 year. The primary endpoint was the 2-year overall survival (OS) rate. Fifty-three patients (98.1%) completed two induction cycles, all 54 proceeded to dCCRT, and 31 (57.4%) received consolidation immunotherapy. Among all 54 enrolled patients, the 2-year OS and progression-free survival (PFS) rates were 84.6% (95% confidence interval [CI], 75.2%-95.0%) and 61.5% (95% CI, 49.5%-76.4%), respectively, after a median follow-up of 28.1 months. Adverse events occurred predominantly during dCCRT and were mainly hematologic; lymphopenia and esophagitis were among the most frequent toxicities. Exploratory analyses suggested that suboptimal response after induction immunochemotherapy was associated with shorter PFS. The survival outcomes observed with this sequential approach support further evaluation of its comparative clinical benefit in randomized studies.
