item.title: Ultrastructural features associated with the dot-like cytokeratin pattern in Merkel cell carcinoma: a spectrum of intermediate filament organization.
item.dc:creator: Krotofil M, Maksymowicz M, Owczarek D, Siednienko J, Wawręty W, Rutkowski P, Szumera-Ciećkiewicz A, Donizy P
item.description:
Authors: Krotofil M, Maksymowicz M, Owczarek D, Siednienko J, Wawręty W, Rutkowski P, Szumera-Ciećkiewicz A, Donizy P
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1852807
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43074841



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The characteristic paranuclear "dot-like" immunohistochemical staining pattern is a hallmark of Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC), yet its ultrastructural correlates and potential biological significance remain incompletely defined. METHODS: We analyzed four MCC cases. Three tumors showed a classic paranuclear dot-like staining pattern with cytokeratins (CKAE1/AE3, CK20), while one tumor lacking this pattern served as a control. Ultrastructural evaluation was performed using transmission electron microscopy on FFPE tissue reprocessed for ultrastructural analysis. RESULTS: In all three tumors exhibiting a dot-like cytokeratin pattern, cytokeratin immunoreactivity displayed a morphological spectrum. In some areas, submembranous or linear perinuclear staining predominated and corresponded ultrastructurally to thick bundles of intermediate filaments arranged along the nuclear envelope. Elsewhere, these bundles appeared condensed into compact, dense fibrillar bodies composed of tightly packed, coiled cytokeratin filaments. In additional areas, less dense fibrillar bodies with reduced filament packing were observed. The relative proportion of tumor cells exhibiting each pattern varied among cases. Nuclear envelope invaginations (nuclear pockets) were also identified as an additional ultrastructural feature with variable frequency, forming pseudo-inclusion-like profiles; however, they did not constitute the structural substrate of the dot-like cytokeratin pattern. The control tumor lacked both dot-like cytokeratin expression and fibrillar bodies. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings support fibrillar bodies as the primary ultrastructural correlate of the classical dot-like cytokeratin pattern in MCC. The coexistence of thick filament bundles, dense fibrillar bodies, and less dense fibrillar bodies suggests a continuum of intermediate filament reorganization rather than discrete categories. These changes may reflect progressive cytoskeletal remodeling and spatial reorganization with potential links to cellular polarization, motility, and cell division. In contrast, nuclear pockets represent a distinct and unrelated ultrastructural phenomenon. Further functional studies are warranted to clarify the biological significance of these observations.

item.title: Postoperative radiotherapy versus systemic therapy alone for locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma following neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Z, Zhao J, Li C, Li Y, Bai Y, Zhang R, Liu C, Liu C
item.description:
Authors: Yuan Z, Zhao J, Li C, Li Y, Bai Y, Zhang R, Liu C, Liu C
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1978264
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43074770



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (nICT) followed by radical esophagectomy is increasingly used for locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (LA-ESCC), but the incremental value of postoperative radiotherapy (PORT) in patients who also receive postoperative systemic therapy remains uncertain. This study evaluated survival outcomes, recurrence patterns, and treatment-related toxicity associated with adding PORT after nICT and surgery. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 336 patients with LA-ESCC who underwent nICT followed by R0 esophagectomy between February 2021 and November 2024. Postoperatively, 93 patients received systemic therapy plus PORT, whereas 243 received systemic therapy alone. Propensity score matching at a 1:1 ratio was performed to balance baseline clinicopathological characteristics, yielding 71 patients in each group. Disease-free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS), recurrence patterns, and treatment-related adverse events were analyzed. RESULTS: After PSM, 142 patients (71 per group) were analyzed. The PORT group demonstrated significantly improved 2-year OS (91.0% vs. 75.5%; HR = 0.409, 95% CI: 0.181-0.925, P = 0.026) and 2-year DFS (74.2% vs. 50.1%; HR = 0.525, 95% CI: 0.303-0.911, P = 0.018) compared to the systemic therapy group. Patients with ypStage III-IV and ypN+ derived the most significant survival benefits. PORT reduced the locoregional recurrence rate from 48.1% to 32.1%, shifting the primary failure mode to distant metastasis (46.4%). Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 18.3% of PORT patients (primarily hematologic), with grade 3 radiation esophagitis occurring in only 1.1%. CONCLUSION: For LA-ESCC patients treated with nICT and surgery, adding PORT to postoperative systemic therapy improves survival and optimizes recurrence patterns with acceptable toxicity. It represents a promising intensification strategy for high-risk patients.

item.title: Prospective comparison of CT- and MRI-based tumor delineation based on intraoperative navigation and spatially annotated pathology in locally advanced midfacial squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Bauer L, Kühle R, Fuchs J, Moratin J, Deng M, Ehle M, Schindehütte R, Schröter P, Stritzke F, Kozyra K, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Bauer L, Kühle R, Fuchs J, Moratin J, Deng M, Ehle M, Schindehütte R, Schröter P, Stritzke F, Kozyra K, et al.
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1884392
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43065419



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Precise tumor delineation is critical for navigation-guided surgery and radiotherapy (RT) in locally advanced midfacial squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are both recommended for staging and provide complementary information. However, quantitative comparisons of CT- and MRI-based tumor contours remain scarce, while a spatial comparison with histopathological data has never been performed. Therefore, we prospectively compared gross tumor volumes (GTV) derived from CT and MRI before navigation-guided surgery and correlated the results with spatially annotated pathology. METHODS: This imaging sub-analysis was conducted within the prospective NAVIGATORR trial (NCT05671458). Fifteen patients with locally advanced midfacial SCC underwent contrast-enhanced CT and 1.5T or 3T MRI (T1w, T2w, DWI) for navigation-based surgery planning. Datasets were rigidly co-registered and an experienced radiologist independently contoured the GTV on CT and MRI while blinded to the other modality. Besides qualitative and volumetric evaluation, spatial agreement was assessed using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and Hausdorff distance (HD). Tumor contours were correlated with spatially annotated intraoperative biopsy locations and histopathological results. RESULTS: Fifteen patients and 109 spatially annotated biopsy locations (19 tumor-positive) were analyzed. MRI was preferred for tumor delineation by the radiologist in all cases, with superior differentiation between tumor and mucosal swelling (73%) and improved soft tissue contrast (67%). MRI based GTVs were significantly larger than CT-based GTVs (median 28.3 ml vs. 16.8 ml; p = 0.02). DSC values demonstrated fair agreement with considerable heterogeneity (median 0.58; IQR 0.47-0.65), and median HD was 16 mm (IQR 12-27 mm). MRI-based contours encompassed numerically more tumor-positive biopsy locations than CT-based contours (6/19 vs. 1/19; clustered McNemar p = 0.20) while including fewer tumor-negative locations (7/90 vs. 10/90; p = 0.53). At patient level, at least one tumor-positive biopsy was located inside the contour in 3/8 (MRI) vs. 1/8 (CT) patients. DISCUSSION: GTV delineation differs substantially between MRI and CT in locally advanced midfacial SCC, and the two modalities provide complementary information. These exploratory findings support the complementary use of MRI and CT for tumor visualization. Clinical implications remain to be shown by the primary endpoint analysis of the NAVIGATORR trial.

item.title: From ancient remedy to modern use: cannabis and cannabinoids in cancer care in the United States.
item.dc:creator: Behl D, Abrams DI, Zylla DM, D'Andre SD
item.description:
Authors: Behl D, Abrams DI, Zylla DM, D'Andre SD
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1878313
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43061359



Abstract:
Cannabis, an ancient plant that has been used for millennia, is increasingly utilized by patients with cancer to alleviate symptoms related to both the disease and its treatment. This complex botanical contains multiple bioactive compounds, most notably delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and cannabidiol (CBD), which interact with the endogenous endocannabinoid system. THC has been studied the most, and synthetic cannabinoids are approved for the management of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting. However, evidence supporting cannabis for other cancer-related symptoms-including chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy, insomnia, appetite stimulation, and non-neuropathic pain-remains limited. CBD alone has not demonstrated consistent or meaningful clinical benefit. Although preclinical data exist, there is no clinical evidence supporting cannabis as a cancer treatment. Cannabis may interact with prescribed medications, particularly with high-dose oral formulations, and its effects on immunotherapy are under investigation. Overall, cannabis is generally well tolerated, though adverse effects can be significant. Use is discouraged in individuals under 25 years of age due to ongoing neurodevelopment, and patients with active psychiatric or cardiovascular conditions should use cannabis only under close clinical supervision.

item.title: Association between postoperative glutamine supplementation and short-term outcomes after ileostomy reversal in patients with colorectal cancer: a retrospective cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Xiao D, Zhou X, Li Q, Xie J
item.description:
Authors: Xiao D, Zhou X, Li Q, Xie J
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1950443
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43060455



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ileostomy reversal is associated with substantial postoperative morbidity despite being considered a relatively minor surgical procedure. Although glutamine supplementation has been investigated in gastrointestinal surgery, evidence regarding its role in patients undergoing ileostomy reversal remains limited. This study evaluated the association between postoperative glutamine supplementation and short-term outcomes following ileostomy reversal in patients with colorectal cancer. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with colorectal cancer who underwent elective ileostomy reversal between January 2015 and December 2025. Patients were classified into the glutamine group, who received postoperative intravenous glutamine supplementation, and the control group. Postoperative outcomes within 30 days, including complications, gastrointestinal recovery, and length of hospital stay, were compared between groups. RESULTS: A total of 183 patients were included, comprising 103 patients in the glutamine group and 80 in the control group. After 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM), 74 matched pairs were identified. Compared with the control group, the glutamine group had a significantly lower incidence of overall postoperative complications (14.9% vs. 29.7%, P = 0.043) and infectious complications (9.5% vs. 23.0%, P = 0.041). The glutamine group also had shorter times to first flatus, first defecation, and initiation of oral diets, as well as lower incidences of postoperative nausea and vomiting and abdominal distension. Hospital stay was shorter in the glutamine group. No significant between-group differences were observed in postoperative serum prealbumin, total protein, or albumin levels. CONCLUSIONS: In this PSM study, postoperative glutamine supplementation was associated with fewer postoperative complications, faster gastrointestinal recovery, and shorter hospital stay following ileostomy reversal in patients with colorectal cancer. These findings indicate a potential association between glutamine supplementation and favorable short-term postoperative outcomes and warrant confirmation in prospective randomized studies.

item.title: Salivary glands auto-segmentation in head and neck radiotherapy: imaging modalities, models, and clinical relevance.
item.dc:creator: Wong WL, Shum CY, Chow YL, Man KH, Law HKW, Tam SY
item.description:
Authors: Wong WL, Shum CY, Chow YL, Man KH, Law HKW, Tam SY
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1923659
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43054526



Abstract:
Radiotherapy-induced salivary gland injury is a major contributor to xerostomia and impaired quality of life in patients with head and neck cancer, making accurate organ-at-risk delineation clinically important. Deep learning-based auto-segmentation has the potential to improve contouring efficiency and consistency, but reported performance is heterogeneous and its clinical significance is not always clear. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on salivary gland auto-segmentation across computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and prostate-specific membrane antigen positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PSMA PET-CT), with particular emphasis on gland-specific challenges, performance evaluation, and clinical translation. CT has the largest evidence base and remains most relevant to routine radiotherapy planning, whereas MRI provides improved soft-tissue visualization and PSMA PET-CT offers high functional contrast for selected salivary structures. Across modalities, segmentation performance is generally more challenging for smaller structures, particularly the sublingual and tubarial gland regions. Importantly, geometric metrics such as the Dice similarity coefficient do not alone establish clinical acceptability or dosimetric equivalence; evaluation should also consider boundary accuracy, expert correction burden, clinical acceptability, and dosimetric impact. Current evidence is further limited by heterogeneous study designs and reference standards, scarce external validation, and limited evidence linking auto-segmentation directly to treatment-related toxicity or patient outcomes. Future research should prioritize multi-institutional validation, clinically meaningful evaluation, improved segmentation of small glands, and human-in-the-loop integration into adaptive radiotherapy. Overall, auto-segmentation represents a promising tool for salivary gland delineation, but its clinical implementation should be supported by evidence extending beyond geometric accuracy alone.

item.title: Radiomics-driven multimodal integration in precision radiotherapy for nasopharyngeal carcinoma- current evidence, clinical barriers, and future directions.
item.dc:creator: Ma Y, Xie Y, Gou Q, Chen N, Gou Q
item.description:
Authors: Ma Y, Xie Y, Gou Q, Chen N, Gou Q
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1902266
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43054349



Abstract:
Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), a head and neck malignancy, is highly sensitive to radiation. Accordingly, radiotherapy has long been the primary curative modality for patients with non-metastatic NPC. Although intensity-modulated radiotherapy has significantly improved target conformality and normal tissue protection, local recurrence, distant metastasis, and late toxicity remain important issues in long-term management. To achieve a balance between tumor control and normal tissue protection, the continuous integration of multi-source information throughout the treatment workflow is critical. Radiomics has the potential to quantify spatial heterogeneity that may not be fully captured by conventional visual assessment. In this review, radiomics-driven multimodal integration refers to the task-specific combination of imaging-derived phenotypes with complementary clinical variables, Epstein-Barr virus DNA (EBV-DNA), hematological biomarkers, dose distributions, pathological features, molecular data, longitudinal imaging, or treatment-delivery information for defined radiotherapy decisions. This review focuses on the clinical timeline of precision radiotherapy for NPC and provides an overview of radiomics-driven multimodal integration studies. It discusses the current applications and limitations of this framework in pretreatment risk stratification and treatment selection, target volume and organ-at-risk definition during radiotherapy planning, on-treatment monitoring and adaptive radiotherapy, toxicity prediction and normal-tissue protection, and post-treatment recurrence assessment and re-irradiation decision-making. This synthesis of current evidence, clinical barriers, and methodological considerations may inform future validation and implementation of radiomics-driven multimodal integration in NPC precision radiotherapy.

item.title: Proton beam therapy in the treatment of adenoid cystic carcinoma of the head and neck: a single enterprise retrospective cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Rohit A, Voss M, Gunn H, Ma D, Patel S, Lester S, Rwigema JC, Neben-Wittich M, Foote R, Routman DM, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Rohit A, Voss M, Gunn H, Ma D, Patel S, Lester S, Rwigema JC, Neben-Wittich M, Foote R, Routman DM, et al.
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1968350
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43054136



Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) is a rare salivary gland malignancy with high propensity for perineural invasion (PNI) and relative radioresistance. Proton beam therapy (PBT) may improve tumor control through improved target coverage, as well as higher physical and biologic dose while limiting dose to surrounding critical structures. This single-enterprise two-site study reports outcomes and toxicity in patients with ACC of the head and neck (HN) region treated with curative-intent PBT. METHODS: From 2015-2025, 89 patients with HN ACC were treated with curative-intent PBT. Patients with distant metastases or prior radiotherapy (RT) were excluded. Clinical outcomes were assessed retrospectively. Toxicities were recorded prospectively using CTCAE v5.0. The Kaplan-Meier method was used to estimate local tumor control (LC), distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS) and overall survival (OS). Hazard ratios, 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and test of association between tumor and treatment variables and outcomes were estimated using Cox proportional hazards regression analysis. RESULTS: Median follow-up was 3.1 years. Sixty-nine patients underwent surgery followed by postoperative PBT, while 20 received definitive PBT for unresectable disease. The 3-year LC rate was 98.3% following postoperative PBT and 82.6% following definitive PBT. Treatment approach was not significantly associated with LC. Three-year DMFS was 86.2% and 64.9%, respectively, while 3-year OS was 94.4% in both cohorts. Twenty-one patients developed distant metastases, most commonly involving the lungs. Six patients experienced acute grade 3 toxicities, including dysphagia, mucositis, and dermatitis; seven experienced late grade 3 toxicities, most commonly osteoradionecrosis (n=4). One patient had both acute and late toxicity. No grade 4 or 5 toxicities occurred. CONCLUSIONS: Curative-intent PBT was associated with favorable LC and acceptable toxicity. Outcomes according to definitive versus postoperative treatment should be interpreted descriptively due to substantial baseline differences between groups and confounding by indication. Longer follow-up and larger studies are needed.

item.title: Pretreatment platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio and survival after definitive radio(chemo)therapy for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: an exploratory cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Werner J, Lehnick D, Strobel K, Stenz NA, Morand GB, Rajan GP
item.description:
Authors: Werner J, Lehnick D, Strobel K, Stenz NA, Morand GB, Rajan GP
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1970136
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43054093



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Current staging provides limited prognostic accuracy in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). We evaluated whether pretreatment systemic inflammatory ratios and 2-deoxy-2-[18F]fluoro-D-glucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography ([18F]FDG PET/CT) metabolic parameters are associated with survival in patients treated with definitive radio(chemo)therapy. METHODS: We retrospectively studied 110 patients with HNSCC treated with definitive radio(chemo)therapy at a single center. Inflammatory ratios, including the platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), were derived from a pretreatment blood count. Metabolic parameters were obtained from staging [18F]FDG PET/CT. The primary endpoints were overall survival (OS) and disease-specific survival (DSS). A Cox model comprising PLR, p16 status, cT category and age was fitted for each endpoint. Missing p16 status was handled by multiple imputation. RESULTS: A higher PLR was independently associated with worse OS (HR per interquartile range 1.61, 95% CI 1.13-2.28; p = 0.008) and DSS (HR 1.78, 95% CI 1.21-2.60; p = 0.003), alongside p16-negativity. cT4 category and age were also independently associated with OS. p16 was missing in 30% of patients, mostly non-oropharyngeal tumors. Complete-case analysis was therefore restricted to 77 patients, in which the point estimates were similar, but the association no longer reached significance. PLR correlated weakly with cT category (Spearman ρ = 0.275, p = 0.004) without collinearity. In exploratory analyses, the association between a high PLR and worse survival was clear in oropharyngeal tumors but weaker in other subsites. Metabolic parameters did not demonstrate an independent association with survival after adjustment. CONCLUSIONS: Pretreatment PLR was independently associated with worse OS and DSS in HNSCC treated with definitive radio(chemo)therapy in the primary multiple-imputation analysis. Effect estimates were consistent in direction and magnitude across all three approaches to missing p16 status. A higher PLR indicates a worse prognosis, but the association is modest and does not guide treatment selection. Prospective validation with prespecified cutoffs is required before clinical use.

item.title: Differences in variant profile between follicular thyroid carcinoma and adenoma: targeted next-generation sequencing study.
item.dc:creator: Lai CC, Chang TA, Chen YJ
item.description:
Authors: Lai CC, Chang TA, Chen YJ
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1902761
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43053988



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Preoperative ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration cytology cannot reliably distinguish follicular thyroid carcinoma (FTC) from follicular thyroid adenoma (FTA), making these neoplasms particularly challenging to diagnose. Although several studies have explored variant differences using targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS) panels, the molecular distinctions between FTC and FTA remain incompletely defined. In this study, targeted NGS was performed on DNA from 52 formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded specimens. METHODS: Genomic DNA was extracted, quality assessed, and targeted NGS performed for 14 genes commonly mutated in thyroid neoplasms. Synonymous variants were excluded, and analyses then focused on pathogenic alterations. Variant frequencies were evaluated at both the locus and gene levels in FTC and FTA. RESULTS: After excluding synonymous variants, 1,074 variants across 14 genes were identified, with 92.8% clustered in five genes: TERT (70.5%), TSHR (8.6%), RET (5.9%), TP53 (4.2%), and BRAF (3.6%). FTC and FTA exhibited distinct variant landscapes, and TERT variants were significantly enriched in FTC. EIF1AX splice site variants (chrX:20148727; c.338-2A>C and c.338-2A>T) were significantly associated with FTC. In the pathogenic dataset, each additional EIF1AX variant increased the likelihood of FTC by 15.4-fold. In contrast, RET and PTEN variants were more frequent in FTA, and each additional RET variant reduced the probability of FTC by nearly half (odds ratio, 0.489). CONCLUSION: These findings underscored the potential diagnostic utility of variant profiling. TERT and EIF1AX variants were predictors of malignant transformation, whereas RET and PTEN variants were more frequently detected in FTA. Their diagnostic and therapeutic utility warrants further validation in clinical settings.

item.title: A systematic review: is contralateral elective neck dissection or neck radiotherapy indicated in lateralised cT3/T4 N0 oral squamous cell carcinoma?
item.dc:creator: Obialo N, Tagdiwala PA, Cassidy O, Schilling C, Eldweny H, Leung B, Bisase B, Norris P, Doumas SN
item.description:
Authors: Obialo N, Tagdiwala PA, Cassidy O, Schilling C, Eldweny H, Leung B, Bisase B, Norris P, Doumas SN
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1944716
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43047546



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Contralateral cervical lymph node metastasis remains a therapeutic challenge in patients with lateralised T3/T4 N0 oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), with current guidelines offering differing recommendations regarding management of the contralateral neck. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA. MEDLINE and Embase were searched from January 2008 to March 2026 for studies evaluating contralateral neck management in lateralised T3/T4 N0 OSCC. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I and QUADAS-2, according to study design. Where possible, a meta-analysis was undertaken by combining outcome measures, otherwise due to anticipated heterogeneity a narrative synthesis was used. RESULTS: Search of the databases revealed 10,670 articles, following deduplication 5,173 were screened and 23 articles were sought for retrieval. Thirteen studies were included, involving 2,764 patients, predominantly retrospective cohorts; 561 were clearly identified as well lateralised T3N0 or T4N0. The tongue was the most common tumour subsite. A random-effects meta-analysis of proportions demonstrated a pooled contralateral neck disease rate of 16.1% (95% CI 1.2-51.7%), the 95% prediction interval was 0.1-90.3%, indicating substantial between-study heterogeneity (I² = 93.5%). Available studies did not provide sufficient evidence to determine whether elective contralateral neck treatment improves locoregional control, disease-free survival or cancer specific survival compared with observation. Interpretation was limited by retrospective study designs, heterogeneity and potential confounding. Sentinel lymph node biopsy and lymphoscintigraphy-guided approaches may help identify selected patients at risk of contralateral disease, although evidence in advanced tumours remains limited. DISCUSSION: Overall, the current evidence is insufficient to support or oppose routine elective contralateral neck dissection or radiotherapy in lateralised T3/T4 N0 OSCC. Selective lymphatic mapping may support more individualised management, but prospective validation is required before its routine use. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, identifier CRD420261499193.

item.title: Comparative effectiveness of five treatment strategies for locally advanced oral squamous cell carcinoma in resource-limited settings: a multinomial overlap-weighted real-world cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Song L, Chen Y, Pan Z, Ma Z, Li J, Jiang L
item.description:
Authors: Song L, Chen Y, Pan Z, Ma Z, Li J, Jiang L
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1993812
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43047457



Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: For locally advanced oral squamous cell carcinoma (LA-OSCC), radical surgery followed by risk-adapted postoperative radiotherapy or concurrent chemoradiotherapy is standard. In resource-limited settings, limited radiotherapy access, costs, and poor tolerance yield multiple pragmatic strategies. Prior real-world studies mostly used pairwise comparisons, lacking systematic evaluation of all coexisting strategies within one framework. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 388 patients with LA-OSCC treated between January 2019 and December 2022, classified into five groups by actual treatment received: surgery with adjuvant chemoradiotherapy (surgery plus CRT), surgery with adjuvant radiotherapy (surgery plus RT), surgery with adjuvant chemotherapy (surgery plus CT), surgery alone, and definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT). Multinomial overlap weighting targeting the average treatment effect in the overlap population (OW-ATO) balanced 10 baseline covariates, and overlap-weighted Cox models with robust variance estimation compared overall survival (OS), disease-free survival (DFS), and disease-specific survival (DSS). Two-group (surgery versus definitive CRT) and four-group (operated patients, pathology-adjusted) analyses, competing-risk models, and sensitivity analyses (IPTW-ATE, landmark, early-death exclusion, E-value, bootstrap) assessed robustness. RESULTS: After overlap weighting, the maximum absolute pairwise standardized mean difference decreased from 0.548 to 0.168. Compared with surgery plus CRT, surgery plus RT showed no statistically significant differences in OS (hazard ratio [HR] 1.33, 95% CI 0.76-2.33), DFS (HR 1.23, 95% CI 0.79-1.90), or DSS (HR 1.56, 95% CI 0.77-3.15), whereas surgery plus CT (OS HR 2.54, 95% CI 1.47-4.39), surgery alone (OS HR 3.21, 95% CI 1.94-5.32), and definitive CRT (OS HR 3.31, 95% CI 1.97-5.57) were each associated with significantly worse outcomes across all three endpoints. Findings were consistent across all analytical layers and sensitivity analyses. CONCLUSIONS: In resource-limited real-world settings, surgery-based multimodal strategies were associated with better survival in LA-OSCC. Surgery plus RT did not differ significantly from surgery plus CRT; however, given wide confidence intervals and limited power, equivalence was not established, and it should be considered only a potential de-escalation option for selected patients who cannot receive concurrent chemotherapy-not as a replacement for standard chemoradiotherapy in high-risk disease. Surgery plus CT should be reserved as a second-best option when radiotherapy is completely unavailable.

item.title: Single-cell and spatially resolved immune profiling in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: a bibliometric and thematic analysis.
item.dc:creator: Li Y, Wang B, Zhang N, Peng G
item.description:
Authors: Li Y, Wang B, Zhang N, Peng G
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1985265
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43047303



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Single-cell and spatially resolved technologies have expanded research on immune heterogeneity in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). We examined relationships among research themes, their cited foundations, and their temporal representation. METHODS: Web of Science Core Collection and PubMed were searched for publications dated from 1900 through July 1, 2026. After deduplication and screening, 587 English-language articles and reviews were included. Bibliometric networks were analyzed using VOSviewer, R, and bibliometrix. Document-level cosine overlaps between keyword and reference clusters were evaluated using stratified permutations with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment. Temporal analyses used keyword proportions and citation-weighted reference-year profiles within three descriptive windows. Sensitivity analyses examined database composition, inclusion thresholds, and individual recent references. RESULTS: Publication output increased after 2021. China had the largest publication output, while the United States had the highest citation count and international-collaboration total link strength. Co-citation and keyword analyses identified four and three domains, respectively. K3-C2 had the largest observed cosine score (0.661), exceeding its null mean by 0.039 (adjusted P = 0.0072); K1-C1 also exceeded its null expectation (adjusted P = 0.0012). Among keyword-available publications, spatial transcriptomics increased from 0.0% to 1.7% and 8.3% across the three windows. The recent reference subset contained five references, all published in 2024; its C2 share was sensitive to individual references. Keyword-cluster agreement was high across database sources and moderate at the stricter occurrence threshold. CONCLUSION: The analysis identifies relationships among immune, cellular, stromal, spatial, and computational literature domains and descriptive changes in keyword representation. These findings provide a quantitative literature framework for further investigation of HNSCC immune profiling.

item.title: Direct Oral Anticoagulant Use and Acute Intracranial Hemorrhage in Adults Undergoing CT After Head Injury.
item.dc:creator: Bloom B, Pott J, Skene I, Astin-Chamberlain R, Caponi N, Fritz CL, Haimovich AD, Thomas SH
item.description:
Authors: Bloom B, Pott J, Skene I, Astin-Chamberlain R, Caponi N, Fritz CL, Haimovich AD, Thomas SH
Journal: JAMA network open | DOI: 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.45624
Published: 2026-Nov-02
PMID: 43071377



Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) therapy is commonly considered a risk factor for traumatic intracranial hemorrhage after head injury, but direct comparisons with no anticoagulation exposure are limited. OBJECTIVE: To assess whether active DOAC exposure, compared with no anticoagulation exposure, is associated with acute intracranial hemorrhage among adults undergoing computed tomography (CT) imaging after head injury. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study was conducted in 3 emergency departments within a large urban National Health Service trust in London, UK. Linked emergency department, hospital, and primary care prescribing records from January 1, 2018, to December 31, 2022, were used. Adults aged 18 years or older presenting with head injury who underwent head CT were eligible. Analysis was conducted between June 2025 and June 2026. EXPOSURES: Active DOAC prescription (including apixaban, dabigatran, edoxaban, or rivaroxaban) at presentation compared with no anticoagulant prescription. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was acute intracranial hemorrhage on initial CT scan. Secondary outcomes were neurosurgical intervention and 28-day mortality. Associations were calculated using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for prespecified confounders. RESULTS: This study included 11 401 episodes in 10 625 unique patients (6652 male [58.3%]; median age, 52 years [IQR, 33-77 years]). A total of 565 episodes (5.0%) occurred in participants prescribed DOAC therapy, and 10 836 episodes (95.0%) occurred in those with no anticoagulant exposure. Acute intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 40 DOAC-treated episodes (7.1%) and 831 non-anticoagulant-treated episodes (7.7%). After adjustment, DOAC exposure was not associated with acute intracranial hemorrhage (adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 0.93; 95% CI, 0.70-1.21). Neurosurgical intervention occurred in 2 DOAC-treated episodes and 44 non-anticoagulant-treated episodes (0.4% in each group, AOR, 1.58; 95% CI, 0.47-4.17). Although crude 28-day mortality was higher among DOAC-treated episodes (17 of 565 [3.0%] vs 185 of 10 836 [1.7%]), adjusted analyses did not show higher odds of mortality (AOR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.46-1.01). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of adults undergoing CT imaging after head injury, DOAC exposure was not associated with higher adjusted odds of acute intracranial hemorrhage, neurosurgical intervention, or 28-day mortality compared with no anticoagulant exposure. However, clinically important differences cannot be excluded.

Published: 2026-Oct-30
PMID: 43051268



Abstract:
Clear aligner therapy poses a particular challenge for orthognathic surgery: the absence of fixed orthodontic attachments compromises conventional intermaxillary fixation, which relies on brackets or skeletal anchorage. We describe FIXED, a CAD/CAM-designed, tooth-bonded intermaxillary fixation device for patients undergoing orthognathic surgery during clear aligner therapy. The device is digitally planned from intraoral scans, 3-dimensional-printed in biocompatible resin, and cemented to the buccal enamel before surgery, providing anchorage for wires and elastics without the morbidity of skeletal screws or the esthetic compromise of temporary brackets. We illustrate the digital workflow, fabrication protocol, and surgical application in 3 patients with Class II and Class III malocclusion, one of them managed with a surgery-first protocol. In all cases, intraoperative fixation was achieved as planned, with no device-related complications during the perioperative period.

item.title: Clinical influence of interproximal wedge positions with a modified image receptor-holding device for bitewing radiography.
item.dc:creator: Ravanelli L, Felizardo HMA, Chang M, Cascante-Sequeira D, Gaêta-Araujo H
item.description:
Authors: Ravanelli L, Felizardo HMA, Chang M, Cascante-Sequeira D, Gaêta-Araujo H
Journal: Oral surgery, oral medicine, oral pathology and oral radiology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oooo.2026.10.014
Published: 2026-Oct-27
PMID: 43052116



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the influence of different positions of the interproximal wedge of a modified image receptor-holding device (IRHD) on proximal surfaces overlapping in intraoral bitewing radiography. STUDY DESIGN: This clinical study included 100 patients who underwent bitewing radiography using four IRHDs: two traditional devices from commercially available kits, and two variations of a modified IRHD (interproximal wedge facing upward-MSW, or downward-MIW). Patients were randomly assigned to the IRHD and interproximal wedge direction on each side of the arch. Images were obtained using a digital radiographic system. Two oral radiologists independently evaluated proximal surface overlap. The overlap rate was expressed as absolute and relative frequencies and compared using the chi-square test with a significance level of 5%. Operator perception and patient comfort were descriptively evaluated using questionnaires. RESULTS: Statistically significant differences were observed among IRHDs (P < .05). The MSW device showed significantly less overlap (P < .05) compared to the other receptor-holding devices across regions and arches. The modified IRHDs achieved higher comfort scores. CONCLUSIONS: The modified IRHD with the interproximal wedge facing upward demonstrated satisfactory clinical performance with less proximal surface overlap and greater patient comfort.

item.title: Gut epithelial aryl hydrocarbon receptor deficiency aggravates fungal dysbiosis-mediated neutrophilic allergic airway disease in mice.
item.dc:creator: Wang T, Lei C, Xu Z, Song X, Tuohongerbieke A, Jones T, Kong M, Hao C, Chen Z, Tan Y, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Wang T, Lei C, Xu Z, Song X, Tuohongerbieke A, Jones T, Kong M, Hao C, Chen Z, Tan Y, et al.
Journal: Nature communications | DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78800-6
Published: 2026-Oct-24
PMID: 43073258



Abstract:
Fungal and bacterial dysbiosis are linked to asthma disease severity, yet how overgrowth of the commensal fungus Candida albicans contributes to disease progression is not fully understood. Here, we show that intestinal aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) deficiency exacerbates house dust mite (HDM)-induced allergic airway disease (AAD) during oral Candida albicans colonization through enhanced IL-17 responsiveness and lung structural cell fucosylation. Intestinal AhR deficiency promotes exaggerated IL-17 responses that promotes neutrophil migration and accumulation in the lung and reshapes the gut microbiota, particularly reducing the abundance of Akkermansia muciniphila. Concurrently, increased fucosylation of lung structural cells enhances L-selectin glycan ligand biosynthesis, thereby promoting neutrophil adhesion and retention within inflamed lung tissue. These adherent neutrophils lead to mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and tissue injury in epithelial and endothelial compartments. Administration of A. muciniphila or its derived outer membrane vesicles (OMVs), as well as genetic deletion of Fut2, reduces lung fucosylation, suppresses neutrophil adhesion and NET formation, and attenuates Candida albicans-exacerbated AAD. Together, these findings show that intestinal AhR signaling remotely regulates an IL-17- gut microbiota-fucosylation axis that promotes neutrophil adhesion, mitochondrial dysfunction of lung structure cell, and neutrophilic airway inflammation during Candida albicans-associated asthma.

item.title: Enterovirus A71 exploits peripheral circulating extracellular vesicles to facilitate blood-brain barrier permeability.
item.dc:creator: Liang Y, Meng Y, Kong Y, Huang S, Zhou Z, Liu S, Zhou X, Zhao F, Wang F, Jin Z, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Liang Y, Meng Y, Kong Y, Huang S, Zhou Z, Liu S, Zhou X, Zhao F, Wang F, Jin Z, et al.
Journal: Nature communications | DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-79119-y
Published: 2026-Oct-24
PMID: 43069275



Abstract:
Enterovirus A71 infection can cause hand, foot, and mouth disease to occasionally develop the severe neurological complications, but how peripheral Enterovirus A71 infection affects the blood-brain barrier remains incompletely understood. Here, we show that Enterovirus A71 infection of peripheral susceptible cells increases the release of extracellular vesicles and promotes the enrichment of microRNA-30 and microRNA-34 within these vesicles. The extracellular vesicle-associated microRNAs suppress Notch1 signaling in human brain microvascular endothelial cells, impair endothelial junctional integrity, and increase blood-brain barrier permeability. Activation of Notch1 signaling restores barrier integrity and reduces viral neuroinvasion in neonatal mice. Clinically, serum extracellular vesicle-associated microRNA-30 and microRNA-34 are elevated in patients with severe Enterovirus A71-associated hand, foot, and mouth disease. Together, our findings identify circulating extracellular vesicles as mediators linking peripheral Enterovirus A71 infection to blood-brain barrier dysfunction and suggest that the microRNA-30/34-Notch1 axis contributes to neurological disease progression during severe Enterovirus A71 infection.

item.title: Peripheral glia drive the initiation of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Micheli S, Salas-Bastos A, Huỳnh K, Cecconi V, Kolm I, Vasilevska J, Debbache J, Renz PF, Diener J, Gwerder M, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Micheli S, Salas-Bastos A, Huỳnh K, Cecconi V, Kolm I, Vasilevska J, Debbache J, Renz PF, Diener J, Gwerder M, et al.
Journal: Nature communications | DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78778-1
Published: 2026-Oct-20
PMID: 43052304



Abstract:
Although tumor innervation is known to promote cancer progression, underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood and have mostly been linked to axonal signaling. Here, we identify peripheral glia as critical drivers of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC), the second most common skin cancer in humans. Tumor-associated glial cells (TAGs) resemble embryonic Schwann cell lineage stages, are abundant in the stroma of premalignant lesions and established murine and human cSCC, and are essential for tumor formation. TAG activation in premalignant lesions is triggered by UV-induced anti-inflammatory macrophages, which in turn are polarized by TAGs into pro-tumorigenic FcεRIα⁺ macrophages, key components of the cSCC microenvironment. Consequently, TAG depletion reduces FcεRIα⁺ macrophages, cancer-associated fibroblasts, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition in keratinocytes, thereby impairing cSCC initiation by disrupting intercellular communication required for tumor development. As most solid tumors are innervated and harbor peripheral glia, our findings reveal TAGs as regulators of tumor initiation with potential relevance beyond skin cancer.

item.title: Large-scale proteomic characterization reveals clinically relevant subtypes of early-stage papillary thyroid cancer for prognostic prediction.
item.dc:creator: Pan J, Ye F, Yao Y, E W, Wang Y, Wu X, Wen S, Zhang Y, Ju F, Chen M, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Pan J, Ye F, Yao Y, E W, Wang Y, Wu X, Wen S, Zhang Y, Ju F, Chen M, et al.
Journal: Nature communications | DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78559-w
Published: 2026-Oct-20
PMID: 43052258



Abstract:
Papillary thyroid cancer (PTC) has a rising incidence. The majority are diagnosed at an early stage, albeit with a minority exhibiting aggressive tendencies. Given its generally indolent nature, controversy persists regarding the management of early-stage PTCs, particularly surgical intervention and long-term surveillance strategies. Here, we conduct a large-scale proteomic characterization of early-stage PTC based on tumor samples from 797 patients. Proteomic profiling unveils clinically relevant modules and identifies six subtypes, capturing the spectrum of heterogeneity from indolent to progressive disease states. Notably, subtypes associated with higher progression risk display enhanced signatures of ribogenesis and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Furthermore, integrating machine learning with protein co-expression network analysis, we identify predictive markers of PTC progression risk such as GPX3 and TMSB4X. Integration of clinical and proteomic data provides a valuable resource for  a deeper understanding of early-stage PTC biology and may inform personalized management strategies for patients with indolent or progressive disease.

item.title: Baseline radiographic and microbiologic predictors of treatment outcomes in a shortened all-oral regimen for MDR/RR-TB.
item.dc:creator: Shen EQL, Mpinda S, Maama L, Tamirat M, Sebakeng P, Oyewusi L, LaHood A, Trevisi L, Romo M, Osso E, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Shen EQL, Mpinda S, Maama L, Tamirat M, Sebakeng P, Oyewusi L, LaHood A, Trevisi L, Romo M, Osso E, et al.
Journal: Nature communications | DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78700-9
Published: 2026-Oct-17
PMID: 43052337



Abstract:
WHO-endorsed shortened, all-oral regimens have improved tolerability and outcomes for MDR/RR-TB treatment, but predictors of poor outcomes remain incompletely-characterized. We conducted a prospective cohort study (NCT05871489) of adults with bacteriologically-confirmed pulmonary MDR/RR-TB treated with a shortened, all-oral regimen in Lesotho. We evaluated baseline microbiologic and radiographic features and their associations with time-to-culture-conversion, end-of-treatment outcomes, and final post-treatment outcomes. Among 238 participants (median age 41 [IQR:31-56], 29% female, 62% with HIV), there were 27 unfavorable outcomes (20 deaths, 3 treatment failures, 4 recurrences). 142 of 148 (95.9%) with positive baseline cultures experienced conversion within four months. Fibrosis, cavitation, bilateral disease, and high smear grade were associated with delayed culture conversion and lower odds of treatment success. Bilateral disease was more strongly associated with unfavorable outcomes in those without HIV; fibrosis and high smear grade showed stronger associations among those with HIV. Cavitation with high smear grade (uOR=0.29, 95%CI:0.11-0.78; aOR=0.39, 95%CI:0.14-1.14), and severe fibrocavitary disease (multi-lobar fibrosis and at least one cavity ≥5 cm) (uOR=0.20, 95%CI:0.07-0.64; aOR=0.26, 95%CI:0.07-0.94) were negatively associated with favorable final outcomes. These findings suggest that baseline sputum and chest radiographic features-particularly in-combination-identify higher-risk patients and may inform risk-adapted strategies for shortened all-oral MDR/RR-TB regimens.

item.title: DigiDent: integrated bristle-level sensing and AI for contact-aware toothbrushing assessment.
item.dc:creator: Ren H, Chang HY, Yu TND, Yang L, Zhang T, Li G, Tang Y, Sang T, Ye Z, Shen Y
item.description:
Authors: Ren H, Chang HY, Yu TND, Yang L, Zhang T, Li G, Tang Y, Sang T, Ye Z, Shen Y
Journal: Nature communications | DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78284-4
Published: 2026-Oct-12
PMID: 43078826



Abstract:
Oral hygiene is fundamental to systemic health, yet toothbrushing, the most common preventive practice, remains largely unguided and unquantified, contributing to the global burden of oral diseases. Current smart toothbrush systems fundamentally fail to capture the critical fine-scale biomechanics at the bristle-tooth interface, which is essential for evaluating clinical adherence and preventing gingival damage. Here we present DigiDent, an AI powered sensing to interpretation system that renders brushing micro-biomechanics computationally interpretable by measuring in-situ contact dynamics at bristle-tooth interface with an embedded E-Bristle sensor. DigiDent fuses bristle-level contact sensing with inertial sensing through a dual-stream neural inference architecture, converting contact-rich brushing behavior into quantitative and interpretable metrics of force, duration, contact-motion pattern, and fine-grained coverage. In validation experiments, DigiDent achieved >99% recognition of motion-contact patterns and 99.84% classification accuracy across 21 brushing subregions. Pilot user-operation verification further demonstrates the feasibility of DigiDent for real-use brushing monitoring and quantitative feedback. These results establish embedded co-deformation sensing and AI-based interpretation as a technical foundation for future personalized toothbrushing assessment and coaching.

item.title: A preliminary nomogram for risk stratification of oral candidiasis in patients with diabetes mellitus: a real-world study.
item.dc:creator: Wang L, Cui Y, Wu S, Wang X, Zhang X, Yan Z
item.description:
Authors: Wang L, Cui Y, Wu S, Wang X, Zhang X, Yan Z
Journal: Oral surgery, oral medicine, oral pathology and oral radiology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oooo.2026.08.019
Published: 2026-Sep-02
PMID: 43067565



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop a clinical nomogram for assessing the probability of oral candidiasis (OC) for risk stratification in patients with diabetes mellitus (DM). STUDY DESIGN: In this retrospective, cross-sectional study among 314 adult patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, OC was confirmed through clinical and mycological evaluation. The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) method and multivariable logistic regression were used to select predictors and construct the nomogram. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), bootstrap-corrected calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA). RESULTS: Of the 314 patients, 174 (55.4%) had OC and 140 (44.6%) did not. Multivariable analysis identified 5 predictors: denture wearing (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 8.92, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.87-27.70), oral hygiene status (aOR 1.66, 95% CI 1.05-2.61), fasting blood glucose (aOR 1.37, 95% CI 1.05-1.77), age (aOR 1.04, 95% CI 1.01-1.06), and male (aOR 0.57, 95% CI 0.33-0.97). The nomogram showed moderate discrimination (AUC 0.732, 95% CI 0.677-0.786), with a bootstrap-corrected calibration slope of 0.854, mean absolute error of 0.020, and Brier score of 0.206, and demonstrated net clinical benefit superior to default strategies across mid-to-high threshold probabilities. CONCLUSIONS: The proof-of-concept nomogram may serve as a practical risk-stratification tool for evaluating OC probability in diabetes patients. These findings are preliminary and prospective external validation is warranted.

item.title: Prognostic model for patients with oral cavity cancer using a novel multi-parameter index including radiation response of patient-derived tumoroids.
item.dc:creator: Jeong E, Choi Y, Lee DW, Lee SY, Bang IJ, Ku B, Lim JG, Jeon SY, Ha P, Jun YW, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Jeong E, Choi Y, Lee DW, Lee SY, Bang IJ, Ku B, Lim JG, Jeon SY, Ha P, Jun YW, et al.
Journal: Radiation oncology (London, England) | DOI: 10.1186/s13014-026-02908-8
Published: 2026-Aug-29
PMID: 43073974



Abstract:
Reliable prognostic models for recurrence after surgery and adjuvant radiation therapy in oral cavity cancer (OCC) remain limited. We developed a tumoroid-based multi-parameter index (MPI) integrating ex vivo radiation-response AUC, tumoroid growth rate, and TNM stage to predict two-year recurrence. Patient-derived tumoroids were established from Korean patients with OCC (n = 16), and the MPI was constructed using multivariable logistic regression. At the prespecified cut-off of 0.5, the MPI achieved 90.00% sensitivity and 66.67% specificity. The apparent AUROC was 0.800, and the optimism-corrected AUROC after 5,000 bootstrap iterations was 0.646 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.467-0.808). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed significant separation in two-year recurrence-free survival between MPI-defined groups (log-rank p = 0.0038). The sensitive group had a significantly lower recurrence risk than the resistant group (hazard ratio, 0.113; 95% CI, 0.020-0.645; p = 0.014). The apparent and optimism-corrected Harrell's C-indices were 0.813 and 0.684 (95% CI, 0.480-0.800), respectively. In an independent, ethnically diverse cohort (n = 4), the MPI correctly classified all recurrence-free and recurrent or progressive cases. These findings support the feasibility of tumoroid-based postoperative prognostic stratification in OCC, although validation in larger independent cohorts is required.

item.title: Expressional patterns of p53: an association with KAISO, clinicopathological characteristics, and field cancerization of OSCC.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed S, Khan S, Qureshi MA, Jamil S, Anis M, Ahmed W
item.description:
Authors: Ahmed S, Khan S, Qureshi MA, Jamil S, Anis M, Ahmed W
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16724-6
Published: 2026-Aug-29
PMID: 43073861



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mutations of the gene TP53 are most frequent among the genetic aberrations found in human cancers. The gene codes for a 43.65 kDa protein that is known to regulate cell cycle, including cell cycle arrest, apoptosis, senescence, DNA repair, or metabolic changes, in response to various cellular stresses. Hence, aberrations in TP53 lead to irregularities in the stress response system and cause cancerous changes in the cells. It has been reported that TP53 activates transcription of KAISO, a ZBTB33 protein, by binding to specific TP53-responsive DNA elements (p53REs) during early DNA damage responses. Significant expression patterns of KAISO have also been reported to play a role in determining field cancerization in oral cancer patients. Therefore, in this study, which was conducted during 2024-25, we have explored expressional patterns of TP53 in relation to KAISO and in terms of field cancerization in oral cancer patients. METHODS: Oral mucosa specimens were acquired from the tumor core, the tumor-free peripheral region after tumor excision, and the opposing non-diseased buccal mucosa of fifty OSCC patients. Normal mucosa samples were taken from fifty patients who volunteered for participation in the study while having elective wisdom tooth removal. Afterwards, specimens were processed for TP53 and KAISO expression using immunohistochemical testing. Image-J software was used to measure the expression, and optical density was calculated from the values obtained from the software. The data obtained was then subjected to statistical analysis. RESULTS: TP53 expression was significantly increased (P-value: <0.0001) in Tumor core, whereas KAISO expression was significantly decreased (P-value: <0.0001) in Tumor core specimens as compared to Periphery (P), opposing mucosa and controls. Similarly, TP53 displayed a significant change in expression in the Nucleus vs. Cytoplasm of the Tumor core (P-Value: 0.0003), which was absent in control specimens, whereas KAISO displayed a significant difference in expression in Nucleus vs. Cytoplasm of Controls (P-Value: <0.0001), which was completely lost in tumor specimens. CONCLUSION: TP53 and KAISO both show an opposing pattern of expression changes from each other in oral cancer patients, which defies the norm of function between the two partners, indicating a possible functional alteration in one or both partner proteins.

item.title: Establishing non-inferiority of rituximab plus lenalidomide in the treatment of advanced previously untreated follicular lymphoma.
item.dc:creator: Perks J, Allen A, Farmer C, Robinson S, Melendez-Torres GJ
item.description:
Authors: Perks J, Allen A, Farmer C, Robinson S, Melendez-Torres GJ
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16836-z
Published: 2026-Aug-29
PMID: 43069117



Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The current standard of care for first-line treatment for people with advanced (stage 3 or 4) follicular lymphoma (FL) is chemotherapy plus rituximab. Rituximab plus lenalidomide is an oral treatment which has been shown to be an effective alternative treatment. In order to support a license extension application for lenalidomide in this indication, NHS England considered the re-analysis of the RELEVANCE trial to determine whether the treatments can be shown to be statistically and clinically non-inferior, before its dismemberment in 2025. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A Bayesian non-inferiority analysis compared rituximab plus lenalidomide with rituximab plus chemotherapy in patients with untreated FL. The primary outcome was overall response rate (ORR). Comparisons to pre-specified non-inferiority margins (- 7% and - 12%) were performed using the intention-to-treat, investigator-assessed population from the RELEVANCE trial. Normal likelihoods were specified using published estimates of the natural history response rate and treatment effect, with default non-informative (flat) priors, and posterior probabilities of exceeding each non-inferiority margin estimated. RESULTS: The posterior probability that rituximab plus lenalidomide was inferior to the pre-specified non-inferiority margins was extremely low post-induction (< 0.01% for - 7% margin and - 12% margin); and at 120 weeks (0.003% for - 7% margin and < 0.01% for - 12% margin). CONCLUSION: The findings are consistent with non-inferiority of rituximab plus lenalidomide compared to rituximab plus chemotherapy for patients with untreated FL when using ORR as the outcome.

item.title: Determinants of a positive resection margin (R1 status) in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: a retrospective analysis of 148,121 cases from China.
item.dc:creator: Han WL, Lei DD, Bao Q, Song X, Xu J, Wei MX, Lei LL, Xu RH, Huang J, Zhang JD, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Han WL, Lei DD, Bao Q, Song X, Xu J, Wei MX, Lei LL, Xu RH, Huang J, Zhang JD, et al.
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16851-0
Published: 2026-Aug-28
PMID: 43079339



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate risk factors for positive proximal and distal resection margins after surgery for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). METHODS: Total initially enrolled esophageal squamous cell carcinoma patients were 148,121 cases. After strict case screening and quality control, a total of 80,881 complete cases were included in the primary analytical cohort, and 29,546 patients from the post-2011 subgroup were further analyzed for sensitivity analysis. Statistical analyses were performed using R4.4.3. Chi-square test was used for intergroup comparisons, and the false discovery rate (FDR) correction was applied for multiple comparisons. Firth penalized logistic regression was adopted for all univariable and multivariable analyses of both proximal and distal margin status across the whole manuscript. RESULTS: Results of the Primary Analysis: Significantly higher positive proximal margin rates were found in patients from low-tier hospitals, low-volume hospitals, males, those aged <60 years, HIA residents, patients with positive family history, cervical+upper tumors, poorly differentiated tumors, T3/T4 lesions, positive lymph node metastasis, advanced TNM stage, multifocal lesions, patients receiving non-minimally invasive surgery, and earlier treatment periods (all P < 0.05). Multivariate adjusted regression confirmed independent risk factors: low hospital volume (20-80: OR=2.158, 95%CI 1.858-2.494, P<0.001; <20: OR=2.804, 95%CI 2.133-3.619, P<0.001), males (OR=1.174, 95%CI 1.070-1.289, P=0.001), poorly differentiated tumors (OR=1.205, 95%CI 1.045-1.392, P=0.010), TNM stage (III: OR=1.315, 95%CI 1.128-1.539, P<0.001; IV: OR=1.754, 95%CI 1.400-2.189, P<0.001) and multifocal lesions (OR=2.459, 95%CI 1.398-4.011, P=0.003). Independent protective factors comprised LIA residence (OR=0.730, 95%CI 0.659-0.809, P<0.001), middle/lower esophageal location (Middle: OR=0.539, 95%CI 0.486-0.600, P<0.001; Lower: OR=0.654, 95%CI 0.572-0.746, P<0.001), and modern treatment eras (2001-2010: OR=0.679, 95%CI 0.569-0.816, P<0.001; 2011-2024: OR=0.509, 95%CI 0.421-0.620, P<0.001); Higher positive distal margin rates were significantly observed in patients from low-tier hospitals, cancer specialized hospitals, HIA regions, rural areas, patients with positive family history, patients receiving non-minimally invasive surgery, and cases diagnosed in earlier time periods (all P < 0.05). Multivariate adjusted analysis identified two independent risk factors: cancer specialized hospitals (OR=1.592, 95%CI 1.269-2.016, P<0.001) and positive family history (OR=1.531, 95%CI 1.260-1.858, P<0.001). Independent protective factors included LIA residence (OR=0.614, 95%CI 0.482-0.776, P<0.001), and the 2011-2024 period (OR=0.298, 95%CI 0.183-0.496, P<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Clinical characteristics differed significantly between patients with positive versus negative proximal and distal surgical margins. Sensitivity analysis verified the robustness of core predictors for positive proximal resection margins. Male sex, TNM stage IV and multifocal lesions remained independent risk factors, while LIA residence and mid/lower thoracic location acted as consistent independent protective factors. Multivariate regression revealed cancer specialized hospitals and positive family history as risk factors for distal resection margin positivity, with LIA residency and 2011-2024 treatment as protective factors, yet this hospital correlation was driven by baseline bias instead of poor surgical quality, and tumor pathology rather than hospital type governed margin status.

item.title: Oral HPV prevalence and its associations with HIV, oral health, immune function, and behavioral factors among youth and mothers in Nigeria: a cross-sectional study.
item.dc:creator: Kumar A, Peter O, Osagie E, Chen J, Akhigbe P, Liu J, Idemudia NL, Kavecky P, Obuekwe O, Udoko FEE, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Kumar A, Peter O, Osagie E, Chen J, Akhigbe P, Liu J, Idemudia NL, Kavecky P, Obuekwe O, Udoko FEE, et al.
Journal: BMC public health | DOI: 10.1186/s12889-026-29077-3
Published: 2026-Aug-28
PMID: 43058613



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: People living with HIV (PLWH) are more susceptible to human papilloma virus (HPV) infection; however, data on the oral HPV burden among youth with or without perinatal HIV exposure or infection in sub-Saharan Africa remain scarce. This study described the distribution of oral HPV and examined demographic, dental, immune and behavioral characteristics of youth and mothers across HIV exposure groups in Nigeria and explored characteristics that co-occurred with oral HPV DNA detection. METHODS: This baseline cross-sectional analysis leveraged data from a prospective cohort in Nigeria. At study enrollment, mothers were categorized as either HIV-infected (HI) or HIV-uninfected (HU), while youth participants were classified as HIV-infected (HI), HIV-exposed uninfected (HEU), or HIV-unexposed uninfected (HUU). Standardized questionnaires were used to capture behavioral data, and comprehensive dental examinations were used to assess decayed, missing, and filled teeth (DMFT), oral hygiene index simplified (OHIS), and gingival inflammation score (GIS). Oral rinse specimens were tested for oral HPV DNA and blood samples were collected for immune parameter assessment (CD4/CD8). The analysis was primarily descriptive given the small number of participants with oral HPV DNA detection. No inferential statistics were performed for HPV-stratified comparisons. RESULTS: In our study, the overall oral HPV prevalence was low and was detected in 7/671 (1%) youth and 8/404 (2%) mothers. Among youth, oral HPV DNA was predominantly detected in HI and HEU groups and exclusively among HI mothers. In descriptive comparisons, youth with HPV DNA tended to have higher CD4 and lower CD8 counts and differences in oral health indices, whereas mothers with HPV DNA reported earlier sexual debut and lower CD4 counts. No inferential statistics were applied to these subgroups. These observations are hypothesis-generating given the small number of participants with detectable HPV DNA. CONCLUSIONS: Despite its low prevalence, oral HPV was detected predominantly among PLWH and co-occurred with certain dental and immunological characteristics in this small number of cases. These findings highlight oral health as a potential area of interest in the context of oral HPV DNA detection and support further investigation into the relationships among oral health, the immune response, and viral detection within the HIV care setting in sub-Saharan Africa but cannot establish causal or predictive relationships.

item.title: Prognostic value of pathological response and nodal status after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Zhang C, Chen Z, Jiang H, Duan X
item.description:
Authors: Zhang C, Chen Z, Jiang H, Duan X
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16811-8
Published: 2026-Aug-27
PMID: 43073794



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To identify prognostic factors for pathological complete response (pCR), disease-free survival (DFS), and overall survival (OS) in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) patients receiving neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (nCIT) followed by esophagectomy. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 441 consecutive patients with locally advanced ESCC who received nCIT followed by R0 esophagectomy at a single high-volume center (2019-2023). Multivariable logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify factors associated with pCR, DFS, and OS. Variables included age, sex, clinical stage, tumor location, chemotherapy type (paclitaxel vs. nab-paclitaxel), PD-1 inhibitor type, number of neoadjuvant cycles, ypT, ypN, tumor regression grade (TRG), number of lymph nodes dissected, and adjuvant therapy. RESULTS: The overall pCR rate was 19.0% (84/441). On multivariable analysis, female sex (P = 0.005), PD-1 inhibitor pembrolizumab (P = 0.003) and tislelizumab (P = 0.003) were independently associated with higher pCR. With a median follow-up of 25 months, independent factors for improved DFS and OS included lower ypN stage, higher number of lymph nodes dissected, and receipt of adjuvant therapy (all P < 0.05). Notably, TRG was independently associated with both DFS and OS in the multivariable model (all P < 0.05). PD-1 inhibitor type and chemotherapy regime was not associated with DFS or OS (all P > 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world cohort, pCR varied by PD-1 inhibitor type, but survival outcomes were primarily determined by nodal status and TRG, rather than ypT status. Extensive lymph node dissection and adjuvant therapy were independently associated with improved survival. These findings underscore the importance of surgical quality, postoperative systemic treatment, and response-based risk stratification in the nCIT era.

item.title: NAT10-mediated ac4C modification and CEBPB-mediated transcriptional activation converge on CBS to promote malignant progression in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Song L, Zhao Q, Yu Y
item.description:
Authors: Song L, Zhao Q, Yu Y
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16817-2
Published: 2026-Aug-27
PMID: 43069066



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is a highly aggressive malignant tumor, and its development mechanism remains unclear. Ferroptosis, as a novel regulatory mode of cell death, plays an important role in tumor regulation. However, the function of cystathionine-β-synthase (CBS) in ESCC and its upstream regulatory mechanism have not been fully elucidated. METHODS: The differentially expressed genes were screened by GEO database (GSE157804 and GSE17351) and PathCards ferroptosis-related protein data. The functions of CBS and its upstream regulatory molecules N-acetyltransferase 10 (NAT10) and CCAAT/enhancer binding protein beta (CEBPB) in ESCC cells were evaluated by quantitative real-time PCR, western blot, Transwell assay, wound healing assay, CCK8 assay, sphere formation assay and detection of ferroptosis-related indexes (Fe2+, GSH, and lipid peroxidation). The intermolecular regulatory relationship was verified by dual-luciferase reporter assay, N4-acetylcytosine (ac4C)-RIP assay, RIP assay, actinomycin D treatment assay, and ChIP assay. A subcutaneous xenograft model in nude mice was established to verify the effect in vivo. RESULTS: By GEO database and PathCards screening, CBS was identified as a important gene that was upregulated in ESCC and was associated with ferroptosis. CBS was highly expressed in ESCC cells (P < 0.05), and its silencing could inhibit ESCC cell invasion, migration, viability and stemness, while promoting ferroptosis (P < 0.05). Mechanistically, NAT10 enhanced CBS mRNA stability and upregulated its expression through ac4C modification (P < 0.05). Transcription factor CEBPB directly bound to the promoter region of CBS to activate its transcription. The recovery of function experiment confirmed that CBS overexpression reversed the inhibitory effect of NAT10 or CEBPB knockdown on ESCC cell malignant phenotype and the promotion effect of ferroptosis (P < 0.05). Furthermore, interference of NAT10 inhibited the growth of ESCC xenografts, while co-overexpression of CBS partially reversed the above effects (P < 0.05). CONCLUSION: Collectively, our findings identify NAT10-mediated ac4C modification and CEBPB-mediated transcriptional activation as two distinct upstream layers that converge on CBS to promote ESCC malignancy and ferroptosis resistance in vitro, providing a mechanistic basis for functional investigation of this axis in ESCC models. In the future, the contribution of ferroptosis to the observed in vivo tumor growth inhibition by NAT10 knockdown remains to be directly demonstrated.
